# Review and reorganize an existing project's folders (agent instructions)

Compare a project that already has content and its own folder structure against the layout below,
recommend improvements, and, only when the user opts in, move content in small reversible batches.
This document is self-contained. For a brand-new project, use [SetupFolders.md](SetupFolders.md)
instead. **Last verified: October 2026.**

## Operating rules

- Start in **review** mode: read and report only. Move nothing until the user has picked items and
  confirmed the exact batch list (stages 3 and 4 below).
- Move imported assets only through Editor APIs (`AssetDatabase.ValidateMoveAsset`, then
  `AssetDatabase.MoveAsset`) or the Project window. Unity ties references to the GUID in each
  `.meta` file, and moving files outside the Editor risks disconnecting the GUID from the file.
  Treat a non-empty string returned by `MoveAsset` as a failure and stop.
- Checkpoints apply to confirmed move batches, not to read-only audit. Continue independent audit
  with user edits and unsaved scenes preserved. Before a move batch, agree a reversible checkpoint
  and resolve edits that overlap its paths; do not stash, commit, or save unrelated work.
- Leave `Packages/`, `ProjectSettings/`, and vendor content with a required layout where they are.
- Keep a move log (old path, new path, GUID) in the conversation; it is the rollback record.
- Stop at the first error, compile failure, or unexpected change. Report it; never push through.
- Mark checks you cannot run **Not verified**.

## Review, recommend, confirm

This document always runs in four stages. Nothing is written to the project until stage 4 ends in an
explicit yes.

1. **Audit.** Read the project and report what already matches this document, what differs, and what
   could not be checked. Read-only.
2. **Recommend.** List every difference as a numbered recommendation: ID, finding, proposed change,
   why it matters, risk (low, medium, high), and a default (do or skip). List items that already
   match as "no change needed". Add recommendations of your own from what you found, including ones
   this document does not mention.
3. **Choose.** The user picks any subset of IDs, "all recommended", or none. Carry over only the
   picked items; unpicked items stay proposals in the report.
4. **Confirm.** Restate the exact changes for the picked subset (files, settings, values, commands)
   and wait for an explicit yes. Make no change before it, including saving the report. In a
   non-interactive session, or when no answer arrives, stop after stage 2 and change nothing.

Steps below that apply, install, or build run only after stage 4, and only for confirmed items. A new
finding during those steps becomes a new recommendation and returns to stage 3.

## 1. Preflight

Read the project's own instructions first; they win over this document. Then record:

- Editor version and whether the Editor is open. Moves need the Editor (or an Editor-driven CLI
  command); a review alone can read the files directly.
- Source-control state, and whether the project compiles cleanly now. Do not start moves on a
  project with compile errors.
- Existing test/compile evidence: record revision, freshness, and known failures. Missing evidence
  is Not verified; new test or compilation runs belong in the confirmed execution plan.
- The `Assets` tree to three levels, with file counts and the longest asset path.
- Template leftovers (`Assets/Settings`, sample scene and assets), vendor folders (Asset Store or
  package-style content with its own layout), and any `Resources`, `StreamingAssets`, `Plugins`,
  `Editor`, or `Gizmos` folders and where they sit.
- Assembly definitions and references, and each script's effective assembly.

**Done:** the inventory and baseline exist, you can state which parts you will treat as vendor, and
nothing has been changed.

## 2. Ask

Ask in one batch. The defaults are recommended answers that still need stages 3 and 4, even when the
user says "use defaults".

| Question | Default |
|---|---|
| Review only, or also reorganize? | Review only |
| Whole project or specific folders or features? | Whole `Assets`, owned content only |
| Adopt the whole layout or only parts? | Parts: keep the project's convention where it is consistent, and fix inconsistencies |
| Move scripts and asmdefs? | No: propose them, move only after separate approval |
| Move path-dependent content (`Resources`, Addressables, `StreamingAssets`)? | No |
| Checkpoint method (commit or stash)? | Commit |

**Done:** the mode and scope are agreed and repeated back in one line each.

## 3. Review against the layout

The target layout, as a menu rather than a mandate:

```text
ArtSource/                # Optional, beside Assets: PSD, Blend, other source files
Packages/                 # Reusable code as embedded packages
Assets/
├── ScriptTemplates/  StreamingAssets/  ThirdPartyAssets/   # direct children when used
├── Settings/Presets/     # Import presets (the starter's convention)
└── {ProjectName}/
    ├── Scenes/  Settings/  Shared/  SceneTemplates/
    └── {Feature}/        # Scenes, Scripts, Editor, Tests, Data, Prefabs, Art, UI
```

Check each area, citing a path as evidence for every finding:

| Area | Look for |
|---|---|
| Organization | Type-first folders (`Scripts`, `Prefabs` at the root) instead of feature-first; duplicate or ambiguous roots (`Scripts` and `Code`); loose assets in the `Assets` root |
| Naming | Spaces, mixed casing, case-only duplicates, dot-prefixed names (Unity skips them on import), accidental `~` suffixes |
| Depth and paths | Nesting beyond about four levels below the content root; very long asset paths |
| Ownership | Content under a feature that other features own, and `Shared` content that depends on feature code or assets; dependency cycles between features |
| Special folders | `StreamingAssets` or `ScriptTemplates` not direct children of `Assets`; `Resources` used for convenience instead of a loading need; `Plugins`, `Editor`, or `Gizmos` placed where they change compilation or behavior |
| Assemblies | Scripts outside any intended asmdef; `Editor` folders inside runtime asmdefs without Editor-only assemblies; test asmdefs that cannot reference production assemblies |
| Vendor content | Vendor files mixed with owned content; vendor files modified in place |
| Source art | PSD, Blend, or other source files inside `Assets` |
| Template leftovers | Unused sample scenes and assets |

Rate each finding **Risk** (likely to cause bugs or build failures), **Improve** (clear benefit), or
**Optional** (taste), and give its **move risk** from the next table.

### Move risk

Moves are safe when only GUIDs refer to the asset, and dangerous where a path, folder name, or
folder position carries meaning.

| Move risk | Content | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Low | Prefabs, materials, textures, models, audio, ScriptableObject assets, UI files, and scenes, moved between ordinary folders | Unity references them by GUID, and the Editor moves the `.meta` file with the asset |
| Medium | Scripts, asmdefs, asmrefs, and anything moved into or out of an `Editor`, `Plugins`, or `Standard Assets` folder | Folder position selects the compile phase and assembly, and an asmdef covers the whole folder tree beneath it, so a move can change which assembly a script belongs to |
| High | `Resources` contents, Addressables, `StreamingAssets` contents, hard-coded `"Assets/..."` strings, import presets and postprocessors scoped by path, CI and `.gitignore` or LFS patterns | Their meaning depends on the path text. Unity's Addressables default address is the asset path, so a moved asset's address can change |
| Leave | `Packages/`, `ProjectSettings/`, vendor content with a required layout, template-created `Assets/Settings`, `Editor Default Resources`, and the special folders themselves | Unity or the vendor expects them where they are |

Before rating anything Medium or High, search the project for `Resources.Load`, hard-coded `Assets/`
paths, Addressables addresses, and path-scoped presets, and record what you find.

**Done:** every finding has evidence, a severity, and a move risk, and every High item has the
code or configuration that depends on it listed. The findings are the audit stage's output.

## 4. Recommend and plan

Present the review: a short summary, the findings table, and what to leave alone, with each finding
as a numbered recommendation (ID, evidence, proposed change, risk, default). Then offer a plan
only if the user asked to reorganize, as ordered batches:

1. Create missing target folders (follow the naming rules: PascalCase, no spaces, no leading dot).
2. Rename and case fixes. On a case-insensitive file system, move a case-only rename through a
   temporary name, and check the result in the Editor.
3. Low-risk content, one feature at a time.
4. Scripts and asmdefs, one assembly at a time (only if approved).
5. High-risk items, only on explicit request and with a stated verification for each.

Each batch lists its moves (old path → new path), the expected effect, the risk, the checks that
prove it, and how to undo it. Keep batches small enough to review: one feature or one assembly.

**Done:** the user has picked specific recommendations and confirmed the exact batches in stage 4,
or chosen review only. The per-batch checkpoints in step 5 stay as extra safety on top of that gate.

## 5. Apply one batch at a time

Only the items confirmed in stage 4 are moved. For each confirmed batch:

1. Checkpoint, then run `ValidateMoveAsset` for every move; resolve any non-empty result first.
2. Move through `MoveAsset`, requiring an empty return each time. Run `AssetDatabase.SaveAssets` and
   `Refresh`, and wait for compilation to finish.
3. Verify (step 6). On success, commit the batch with the move log in the message.
4. On any failure, undo the batch by moving the assets back through `MoveAsset` using the move log.
   If the Editor state is unreliable, close it and restore the checkpoint with source control.

**Done:** the audit and recommendation list were shown and confirmed before batch 1, and the batch is
committed with verification passed, or fully undone with the cause reported.

## 6. Verify each batch

- Every moved asset keeps its GUID (`AssetDatabase.AssetPathToGUID` before and after).
- The project compiles with no new errors, and each moved script's effective assembly is unchanged
  (compare before and after, for example with `CompilationPipeline.GetAssemblyNameFromScriptPath`).
- Open the scenes and prefabs of the affected features: no missing references or scripts.
- The build scene list still points at existing scenes. Check it; do not assume it updated.
- The project's tests pass, matching the baseline, and Play Mode starts the affected scenes.
- Path-dependent items found in step 3 still resolve: `Resources.Load` names, string paths,
  Addressables addresses, preset and postprocessor filters, CI and ignore patterns.
- After script or assembly batches, a build for a representative player target compiles.

**Done:** each check is Passed, Failed, or Not verified, and any failure has been undone or fixed.

## 7. Report

| Item | Status | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| Each finding | Risk / Improve / Optional | Path, evidence, recommendation, move risk |
| Unpicked recommendations | Proposal | ID and reason left open |
| Each batch | Applied / Undone / Not started | Moves, commit, checks |
| Each check | Passed / Failed / Not verified | Evidence |
| Left alone | Vendor / Leave | Path and reason |

Put open questions, unpicked recommendations that need a ruling, and failed checks in a
"Needs your decision" block at the top.

- [Special folders and script compilation order](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/SpecialFolders.html)
- [AssetDatabase.MoveAsset](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/AssetDatabase.MoveAsset.html)

- [Custom package layout](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/cus-layout.html)

# Set up project folders (agent instructions)

Scaffold the owned-content folders of a newly created Unity project. This document is
self-contained and creates directories only: presets, script templates, scenes, asmdefs, packages,
project settings, and copied guides are separate tasks. Use the tools you already have; install
no package, CLI, or setup script. **Last verified: October 2026.**

## Operating rules

- Create the selected missing directories and nothing else. Never generate `.meta` files, move,
  rename, or delete existing content, or create suffixed duplicates to dodge a conflict.
- The target project's own instructions take precedence over this document.
- Leave existing assets, instructions, and unsaved work untouched.
- When required instructions cannot be read, stop before creating anything rather than working
  from memory. Report the source URL or path you followed.
- Report folder creation and Unity import verification as two separate results.

## Review, recommend, confirm

This document always runs in four stages. Nothing is written to the project until stage 4 ends in an
explicit yes.

1. **Audit.** Read the project and report what already matches this document, what differs, and what
   could not be checked. Read-only.
2. **Recommend.** List every difference as a numbered recommendation: ID, finding, proposed change,
   why it matters, risk (low, medium, high), and a default (do or skip). List items that already
   match as "no change needed". Add recommendations of your own from what you found, including ones
   this document does not mention.
3. **Choose.** The user picks any subset of IDs, "all recommended", or none. Carry over only the
   picked items; unpicked items stay proposals in the report.
4. **Confirm.** Restate the exact changes for the picked subset (files, settings, values, commands)
   and wait for an explicit yes. Make no change before it, including saving the report. In a
   non-interactive session, or when no answer arrives, stop after stage 2 and change nothing.

Steps below that apply, install, or build run only after stage 4, and only for confirmed items. A new
finding during those steps becomes a new recommendation and returns to stage 3.

## 1. Preflight

Identify the target: the user's destination, or the current workspace when it is exactly one Unity
project (it contains `Assets` and `ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt`). Resolve an ambiguous
destination before writing. This starter repository is not a Unity project.

Inspect the existing folders under `Assets`, any established owned-content root, source-control
changes when available, and whether the project's Editor is open.

Look for what the Unity template left behind. Template-created projects arrive with a
`Assets/Settings` folder (its contents depend on the template, for example render pipeline and volume
settings) and often a sample scene and sample assets. List what exists by inspection, and do not
assume names. Reuse `Assets/Settings` as it stands; leave sample content in place and report it.

Check the project's location. The full path and project name should contain no spaces, and the
project should sit close to the drive root on Windows: [reported path-length failures](https://discussions.unity.com/t/unity-editor-still-hits-windows-max-path-260-char-limit-even-with-longpathsenabled-any-real-fix/1732098)
hit IL2CPP and Android builds, and Unity publishes no safe limit. Warn the user when the path is long
instead of moving the project.

**Done:** the target project, local rules, existing folders, template leftovers, path length, and
Editor state are known, and nothing has been created.

## 2. Ask

Ask only what changes the result, in one short round. The defaults are recommended answers: they
become recommendations that still go through stages 3 and 4, even when the user says "use defaults".

| Question | Default |
|---|---|
| Owned-content root name? | An existing root if one is established; otherwise `Assets/{ProjectName}`, using the project directory's name |
| Which real features exist now, and what does each need next? | None: create the root alone |
| Project-wide `Scenes`, `Settings`, or `Shared`? | Only for a responsibility the user selects |
| `Tests/EditMode` and `Tests/PlayMode` folders? | No |
| `Resources`, `Plugins`, or `StreamingAssets`? | No: create only for an actual loading, plugin, or raw-content requirement |
| Extra feature subfolders (`Audio`, `Animations`, `VFX`, `Materials`)? | None: add per feature when content of that kind exists |
| Keep source art files (PSD, Blend, and similar) in the project? | No. When yes, use a project-root `ArtSource` folder beside `Assets`, outside the import pipeline |
| Reusable code to share across projects? | No. A local package is a separate task, not part of folder scaffolding |
| Sample content from the template? | Leave it in place and report it |

**Done:** every proposed directory has a stated purpose and a concrete path under the target `Assets`,
or is the explicitly selected project-root `ArtSource` beside `Assets`.

## 3. Choose the layout

Use this tree as a menu. Each branch that fits the project becomes a numbered recommendation, with
its purpose and risk; `Inventory` and its UI files are an example feature, not scaffolding to copy.

```text
ArtSource/                # Optional, beside Assets: PSD, Blend, and other source files Unity should not import
Packages/                 # Unity-managed; embedded packages live here (separate task)
Assets/
├── ScriptTemplates/      # Selected .cs.txt files (separate task); must be a direct child of Assets
├── StreamingAssets/      # Optional raw player content; must be a direct child of Assets
├── ThirdPartyAssets/     # Vendor imports whose layout permits relocation
├── Settings/Presets/     # Selected import presets (separate task); a starter convention, not a Unity special folder
└── {ProjectName}/
    ├── SceneTemplates/   # Optional source scenes/templates and shared resources
    ├── Scenes/           # Bootstrap, composition, and other project-wide scenes
    ├── Settings/         # Project-wide URP, Input Actions, shared UI settings
    ├── Shared/           # Independent shared code and content
    └── Inventory/        # Example feature; create the real ones
        ├── Scenes/       # Optional feature-owned, test, or demo scenes
        ├── Scripts/
        ├── Editor/
        ├── Tests/        # Optional; EditMode/ and PlayMode/ subfolders
        ├── Data/         # Authored configuration assets
        ├── Prefabs/
        ├── Art/          # Models, textures, materials; add Audio/, Animations/, VFX/ when used
        └── UI/           # UXML, USS, and C# for a screen together; Sprites/ for UI sprites
```

Name every folder you create in PascalCase, with no spaces and consistent casing. Do not start a
name with a dot: the Editor's create menu turns a leading dot into an underscore, and Unity ignores
dot-prefixed folders when importing. Unity also ignores folders ending in `~` and folders named
`cvs`, so use that suffix only when you intend the contents to stay out of the project (for example
`Documentation~`). Keep nesting shallow: aim for at most four levels below the owned-content root.
Those naming and nesting limits are this guide's recommendations, not Unity requirements.

Apply these ownership rules when placing a folder:

- Put code, configuration, and content with the feature that owns its meaning, even when another
  feature consumes it. Multiple consumers alone do not make something shared.
- Use `Shared` only for content with an independent responsibility that depends on no feature
  implementation, through code or asset references.
- Use project-level `Scenes` and `Settings` for composition and configuration that spans features.
- Keep guides, build outputs, and validation reports outside `Assets`.
- Create `Resources` or `Plugins` only for an actual loading or plugin requirement, and honor
  platform-specific plugin paths. Custom Android Gradle templates and a custom main manifest
  belong in `Assets/Plugins/Android/`; Unity generates them when the matching Publishing Settings
  option is enabled, so enable the option instead of creating the files by hand. See the
  [mobile build setup](../BuildSettings/MobileBuilds.md).
- Keep reusable cross-project code out of `Shared`. Unity's custom-package layout (a folder with a
  `package.json`, plus `Runtime`, `Editor`, and `Tests`) in `Packages/` is the supported home for it;
  do not create `package.json` files in this workflow.
- Keep source art in `ArtSource`, beside `Assets`, instead of importing it.
- Defer `Assets/Settings/Presets` and `Assets/ScriptTemplates` to their own workflows.
- Folder creation does not configure test assemblies or asmdefs, and it does not create placeholder
  files or a permanent setup report to keep empty folders alive.

**Done:** the recommended project-relative paths are listed and shown to the user, who has picked a
subset and confirmed it in stage 4. Stop to ask about unresolved choices or conflicts.

## 4. Check, then create

Only the items confirmed in stage 4 are created. Check the complete confirmed path list before
changing anything:

- Each name is a valid single directory segment on the target platform. Reject absolute names,
  separators, `.` and `..`, and case-only collisions with selected or existing paths.
- Every destination resolves inside the intended project's `Assets`, or is the selected project-root
  `ArtSource`. Do not create through a symlinked entry inside `Assets`.
- Reuse an existing directory with matching name and casing. A file at a requested directory path,
  or metadata for a missing directory, is a conflict to resolve before creating anything.

Choose the route by Editor state:

- **Editor closed:** create only the selected missing directories with ordinary filesystem
  operations. Unity generates their metadata on import.
- **Editor open:** use Editor access you already have (for example an `AssetDatabase` folder API),
  checking for each folder before creating it, and target the project explicitly. When no such
  access exists, ask the user to close that project's Editor. Never install a bridge or close an
  Editor with unsaved work.
- **Established project with its own structure:** stop. This document does not review or move
  existing content; hand the user [ReviewFolders.md](ReviewFolders.md) instead.

If a failure interrupts creation, report the paths already created. A rerun must reuse them and
create only the remaining selected directories.

**Done:** the audit and recommendation list were shown and confirmed before any change, and each
confirmed path is Created or Already present, with existing content and metadata unchanged.

## 5. Verify

- Read back every selected path and confirm it is a directory with the intended casing.
- Repeat the missing-folder check; it must find nothing to create.
- Compare before and after. Only the selected directories and Unity-generated folder metadata belong
  to this run. Preserve unrelated concurrent edits.
- After an observed Unity import, confirm that the new folders under `Assets` have generated
  metadata (folders ending in `~` and `ArtSource` get none, by design), GUIDs are unique, pre-existing metadata is unchanged, and the import log has no fresh errors. Open the project
  for import only when a safe route exists and doing so is within scope; otherwise mark the import
  checks **Not verified** and tell the user to open the project in Unity.
- Run no gameplay tests or player build for empty-folder scaffolding.

Empty directories may not survive source control. Commit Unity-generated metadata together with the
folders once it exists.

**Done:** directory verification passes, a repeat run has nothing to add, and the import result is
Verified or Not verified.

## 6. Report

| Item | Status | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| Target project, content root, source URL | | |
| Audit and recommendations shown, confirmation received | Yes / Stopped before confirming | Items picked |
| Unpicked recommendations | Proposal | Path and reason |
| Template leftovers (`Assets/Settings`, sample content) | Reused / Left in place | What exists |
| Project path | OK / Warned | Length and spaces |
| Each selected path | Created / Already present / Conflict | Path |
| Missing-folder recheck | Passed / Failed | |
| Unity import and metadata | Verified / Not verified | Next action if pending |

Put unresolved conflicts, unpicked recommendations that need a ruling, and open choices in a
"Needs your decision" block at the top.

## References

- [Special folder names](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/SpecialFolders.html)
- [Default project directories](https://docs.unity.com/en-us/engine/6000.6/manual/get-started/project-configuration/default-directories)
- [Custom package layout](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/cus-layout.html)
- [Organizing your Unity project](https://unity.com/how-to/organizing-your-project)
- [Assembly definitions](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/assembly-definitions-intro.html)
- [StreamingAssets](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/StreamingAssets.html)

64fa943fa76f8ce76f3b574871d47667e81c05d6.text:
> How it works: give this URL to your agent, for example "Install the import presets I need from
> this document into my Unity project". The agent audits your project first and recommends
> presets, lets you pick which to carry over, and changes nothing before you confirm the exact list.
> It then installs only those presets and, if you choose, applies them to existing assets or
> registers them as defaults. Human overview: [readme](README.md).

# Set up import presets (agent instructions)

Install selected import presets into an existing Unity project and, only when the user asks,
apply them to existing assets or register them as default import rules. This document is
self-contained; it fetches the preset files from the source below. **Last verified: October 2026.**

Source (replace `main` with a commit SHA for a repeatable run):
`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/krogh-jacobsen/unity-code-style-guide/main/AuditInstructions/Presets/`
Each preset is two files, `<Role>/<Name>.preset` and `<Role>/<Name>.preset.meta`. The license is
`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/krogh-jacobsen/unity-code-style-guide/main/LICENSE`.

## Operating rules

- Do three separate things only when selected, in this order: **install** (copy files),
  **apply** (change existing asset importers), **register** (future-import rules). Install is the
  recommended default.
- Copy shipped bytes and metadata unchanged. Never author, edit, or regenerate a `.preset` or its
  `.meta`, never invent GUIDs, and never delete metadata to force a re-import.
- The presets are tuned for desktop PC and Mac games (Windows and macOS standalone). When the
  project also targets mobile, Web, console, or VR, tell the user the audio and model policies were
  not reviewed for those targets and ask before applying them; the texture role presets are
  platform-neutral.
- Preserve the target's own instructions, unsaved work, vendor assets, and customized importers.
- Do not apply a preset to vendor or third-party assets, or to anything outside owned folders.
- Report observed results separately from checks you could not run (**Not verified**). Copying a
  preset proves a file arrived, not that any policy took effect.

## Review, recommend, confirm

This document always runs in four stages. Nothing is written to the project until stage 4 ends in an
explicit yes.

1. **Audit.** Read the project and report what already matches this document, what differs, and what
   could not be checked. Read-only.
2. **Recommend.** List every difference as a numbered recommendation: ID, finding, proposed change,
   why it matters, risk (low, medium, high), and a default (do or skip). List items that already
   match as "no change needed". Add recommendations of your own from what you found, including ones
   this document does not mention.
3. **Choose.** The user picks any subset of IDs, "all recommended", or none. Carry over only the
   picked items; unpicked items stay proposals in the report.
4. **Confirm.** Restate the exact changes for the picked subset (files, settings, values, commands)
   and wait for an explicit yes. Make no change before it, including saving the report. In a
   non-interactive session, or when no answer arrives, stop after stage 2 and change nothing.

Steps below that apply, install, or build run only after stage 4, and only for confirmed items. A new
finding during those steps becomes a new recommendation and returns to stage 3.

Here, steps 1 and 2 are the audit and the recommendations; steps 3 to 6 run only for confirmed items.

## 1. Preflight

Read the target's instructions. Identify one Unity project: the user's destination or the current
workspace, containing `Assets` and `ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt`. Record:

- Editor version, whether that Editor is open, and source-control state.
- Target platforms (Build Profiles and the active build target), to apply the desktop rule above.
- Existing contents of `Assets/Settings/Presets/` and any presets already registered under
  Project Settings > Preset Manager.
- Whether the project has a Unity-template `Assets/Settings` folder (reuse it as it stands).
- The source revision you will use. Resolve `main` to a commit when you can and report it.

**Done:** the target, Editor state, existing presets, and source revision are known, and the audit
(stage 1) was reported without writing anything.

## 2. Ask and select

Ask in one batch. Each default is the recommendation for that question; it takes effect only after
stage 4, even when the user says "use defaults".

| Question | Default |
|---|---|
| Which operation: install only, apply to existing assets, or register defaults? | Install only |
| Which asset roles do you have: textures (albedo, normal, mask, UI sprite), audio (music, ambience, SFX, UI), static models, animation-only? | Only roles with real content in the project |
| For apply or register: which owned folders? | None; ask for exact folders |
| Which audio policy for each kind of clip? | One policy per clip; ask when unclear |
| Separate platform texture/audio budget review? | No; optionally recommend the handoff in step 6 |

Select presets from this inventory. Fetch only the selected pairs; do not copy the whole folder.

| Preset (path under the source) | Use | Policy | GUID |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Textures/AlbedoTextureImporter` | Tiling world color | Default texture, sRGB, mipmaps, repeat, bilinear; CPU read off | `f61eb0483155c4510af0ab38dfedddf2` |
| `Textures/NormalTextureImporter` | Tangent-space normals | Normal map, linear, mipmaps, repeat, bilinear; CPU read off | `e909e14824a2d4c7bbbddfffaad65823` |
| `Textures/MaskTextureImporter` | Packed linear material data | Default texture, linear, mipmaps, repeat, bilinear; CPU read off | `c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6e7f8a9b0c1d2e3f4` |
| `Textures/UISpriteTextureImporter` | Screen-space UI sprites | Sprite, sRGB, no mipmaps, clamp, bilinear, alpha transparency; CPU read off | `2e363ae08c3a848c7854d798a8dd05f2` |
| `Audio/MusicAudioImporter` | Long music | Streaming, Vorbis 0.7; background load | `6ad43c7dea473466bb6e33ba84426394` |
| `Audio/AmbienceAudioImporter` | Long ambience loops | Streaming, Vorbis 0.7; background load | `2ab0a5b23622b46e691e0ba9fba25ecf` |
| `Audio/SFXAudioImporter` | Short, frequent effects | Decompress on load, Vorbis 0.7; preload | `b5cd1643fcc1e4237a3652bde885ab25` |
| `Audio/UIAudioImporter` | Short UI feedback | Decompress on load, Vorbis 0.7; preload | `d7473bccbe2ca42bba6967e205d90af3` |
| `Audio/UIShortAudioImporter` | Tiny UI clicks where codec artifacts matter | Decompress on load, PCM; preload, foreground load | `3f34697a999664156938eab0b9439b00` |
| `Audio/SpatialSFXAudioImporter` | Noisy repeated positional effects | Compressed in memory, ADPCM, force mono; preload, foreground load | `22dbbcb91dde34dc39cbf56beb605c18` |
| `Audio/LayeredAmbienceAudioImporter` | Short overlapping ambience loops | Compressed in memory, Vorbis 0.7; preload, background load | `370ad86a5eb1d47e9a43f258a1e6e80e` |
| `Models/FBXModelImporter` | Static meshes with external materials | No animation, no generated colliders, read/write off; material creation off | `5fbe9a9b7b7441dea18aa7fce90c4820` |
| `Animations/FBXAnimationImporter` | Animation-only source with an existing rig | Import animation; preserve rig, clips, avatar, geometry, materials, scale | `a1c8dd08508c4341a75ed3fd45a1bfd5` |

Rules for choosing:

- Choose **one audio policy per clip**; the audio presets are alternatives, not layers. UIShort suits
  tiny clicks when PCM size is acceptable. SpatialSFX suits noisy overlapping positional effects, and
  forces mono (keep stereo for authored stereo beds and music). LayeredAmbience suits short loops that
  would otherwise create many streams; use Ambience for long beds.
- Keep the animation-only preset distinct from a character or rig import policy.
- **Models:** the FBX Model preset turns Read/Write off. Unity requires Read/Write on for meshes used
  by a Mesh Collider, a Particle System shape, or a Terrain detail mesh, or the Player build can
  fail. Before applying, ask which meshes need those uses and exclude them (or re-enable Read/Write).
- **Audio length:** SFX and UI decompress on load (Vorbis then takes about ten times its compressed
  memory), so use them only for short clips. For longer or numerous effects choose Spatial SFX or
  Layered Ambience.
- **Textures:** alpha-cutout textures (foliage) also need mip preserve-coverage, which the Albedo
  preset does not set; pixel-art sprites need point filtering and are outside these presets.
- Each preset is partial: it includes only its listed policy and preserves everything else, including
  user data, bundle labels, external mappings, and platform overrides.

Turn the answers into numbered recommendations (stage 2): one per preset worth installing (only for
roles with real content), one each for applying to existing assets, registering defaults, and a separate platform-budget
review handoff (step 6). Give each its finding from the audit, why it matters, risk, and a default. The user
may pick any subset (stage 3), then confirms the exact list (stage 4).

**Done:** the recommendations were shown, the user picked from them, and the selected presets, the
operation, and any exact target folders or assets were confirmed before any file was written.

## 3. Install

Only the presets confirmed in stage 4. Stage first, then check, then copy.

1. **Stage.** Download each selected `.preset` and `.preset.meta` into a temporary folder outside
   the target's `Assets`, plus the license. URL-encode filenames with spaces. Reject HTML or error
   responses, and any pair that is missing a half.
2. **Verify.** Each `.meta` must contain the `guid:` from the table above. Stop on a mismatch.
3. **Preflight destinations.** Each preset installs to `Assets/Settings/Presets/<Role>/<Name>.preset`
   (keep the role subfolder), with its `.meta` beside it. Reject path traversal, symlinked entries,
   and case-only collisions. Check each GUID against existing project assets, including package assets.

   | Destination state | Action |
   |---|---|
   | Absent and the GUID unused | New: install |
   | Same bytes and GUID at the path | Already installed: leave it |
   | Different content or GUID, a half pair, or the GUID elsewhere | Conflict: report both paths and resolve before copying |

4. **Copy.** With the target's Editor closed, create only missing directories and copy the staged
   pairs intact; Unity generates metadata for the new folders. With the Editor open, use an
   approved route that preserves the pairs, or ask the user to close the project's Editor. Install
   no bridge or package, and never overwrite an imported or customized preset.
5. **License.** Place the MIT license in the project's existing third-party notices location outside
   `Assets`, or at `ThirdPartyNotices/UnityCodeStyleGuide-LICENSE.txt`. Reuse an identical notice;
   preserve unrelated ones.
6. **Import and read back.** Import through existing Editor access, or open the project when that is
   safe and in scope. Read each installed asset's bytes and GUID; check the logs for fresh errors.
   A repeat run must plan no copies. With no safe import route, report files copied and import
   **Not verified**, with the next action.

**Done:** every selected pair is installed or already present, the license is placed, a repeat run
does nothing, and import has an observed result or an explicit pending check.

## 4. Apply to existing assets (only when selected and confirmed)

Only the targets confirmed in stage 4. Preview the exact owned asset paths and each preset's role before changing anything; resolve
overlapping or incompatible mappings first. Run the procedure through an Editor method driven by
Unity CLI or an available C# execution command (discover the installed commands; the CLI has no
universal preset subcommand):

1. Load the preset with `AssetDatabase.LoadAssetAtPath<Preset>()` and get the target's
   `AssetImporter`. Require `preset.CanBeAppliedTo(importer)`.
2. Record each target's GUID, platform overrides, metadata, and designer-authored values (slices,
   borders, pivots, material mappings, rigs, clips, scale).
3. Call `preset.ApplyTo(importer)` and require success, then `importer.SaveAndReimport()`. For an
   unconfigured UI sprite choose Single (one icon) or Multiple (a sheet, with slicing) explicitly,
   and preserve an existing mode and geometry.
4. Read the importer back after the reimport: intended values present, preserved values unchanged,
   GUIDs unchanged. Check a representative scene or prefab that references the asset.

Never delete metadata or use the Inspector's Reset to apply a policy. On a rerun, skip targets that
already match. With no available Editor route, leave importers untouched and report Not verified.

**Done:** each target matches its policy after reimport, preserved values are intact, and any
unperformed application is stated.

## 5. Register as defaults (only when selected and confirmed)

Only the rules confirmed in stage 4. Default presets apply when Unity imports an asset or creates a component, and only to new imports;
they do not reconfigure assets that already exist. Configure them in Project Settings >
Preset Manager, or by script with `Preset.GetDefaultListForType` and
`Preset.SetDefaultPresetsForType(PresetType, DefaultPreset[])`.

- Scope every filter to owned folders. A filter matches file names, folders, and extensions, and a
  `glob:` prefix enables case-sensitive glob patterns. Preview what each filter matches first.
- Order matters: entries apply top to bottom and later entries override earlier ones. Read the existing
  list, preserve unrelated rules, reuse a matching registration, and never add duplicates on a rerun.
- **Textures on Unity 6000.7.0b4:** registering texture defaults crashed Unity during first import.
  On that version, import the texture first, then apply the preset explicitly (step 4). Treat any
  other Editor version as unverified until a fresh texture import succeeds there. Audio and model
  defaults passed on that version.
- Verify with a genuinely new asset imported into a filtered folder, then remove the test asset
  through Editor APIs. Install no `AssetPostprocessor` or other enforcer; persistent enforcement is a
  separate project decision.
- If a safe new-import test is unavailable, keep the files and report registration as unvalidated.

**Done:** the selected rules are saved, a new import shows the intended policy, and unrelated rules
are untouched, or the unperformed check is stated.

## 6. Platform budgets (separate selection)

The role presets set data meaning and sampling; they preserve existing resolution, compression, and
platform overrides. Audit those overrides without choosing new budgets in this standalone workflow.
When the user wants budget tuning, recommend a separate build-guide handoff:
[desktop](../BuildSettings/DesktopBuilds.md) or [mobile](../BuildSettings/MobileBuilds.md). That workflow
owns device requirements, measurements, exact values, and confirmation. Missing sibling guidance
never blocks preset installation, application, or registration; no budget change is implied here.

**Done:** existing overrides remain preserved and any requested budget tuning is identified as a
separate recommendation/handoff, rather than an incomplete preset operation.

## 7. Report

| Item | Status | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| Source URL and revision | | |
| Each selected preset | Installed / Already installed / Conflict | Path and GUID |
| License | Placed / Already present | Location |
| Repeat run | Nothing to do / Work found | |
| Unity import | Verified / Not verified | Next action if pending |
| Apply to assets | Applied / Not selected / Not verified | Targets and readback |
| Register defaults | Registered / Not selected / Not verified | Filters, order, new-import result |
| Unpicked recommendations | Proposal | IDs, with the reason each was skipped |

Put conflicts, unanswered choices, unpicked recommendations, and failed checks in a "Needs your
decision" block at the top.

## References

- [Presets](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/Presets.html)
- [Preset Manager settings](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/class-PresetManager.html)
- [Preset API](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Presets.Preset.html)
- [Texture formats](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/texture-formats-reference.html)
- [Audio clip import settings](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/class-AudioClip.html)

> How it works: give this URL to your agent, for example "Review my Unity project's settings
> against this document". The agent audits first and recommends changes; you pick which to carry
> over, and nothing changes until you confirm. Works on any Unity 6 project. Human overview:
> [readme](README.md).

# Project settings review and setup (agent instructions)

Check a Unity project's core settings against a safe starting policy, report the gaps, and, only
when the user approves, apply them. This document is self-contained. Values are starting choices,
not performance claims: keep a setting that already works unless the user selects the change.
**Last verified: October 2026**, against the Unity 6.7 beta manual. That manual has no 6.7
"what's new" or upgrade page yet, so re-check rows marked **6.6+** when 6.7 ships.

## Operating rules

- Start in **review** mode (stages 1 and 2 below): read and report only. Apply nothing until stage 4
  ends in an explicit yes.
- Change settings through Editor APIs or Unity CLI (`EditorSettings`, `PlayerSettings`,
  `QualitySettings`, `GraphicsSettings`, `SerializedObject`) or the Project Settings window. Never
  hand-edit `ProjectSettings/*.asset` or `.meta` files.
- Read every value before changing it and read it back after saving. Confirm each API name against
  the installed Editor; those below are the Unity 6 shape.
- Continue independent read-only audit with existing edits preserved. Establish an attributable
  baseline or isolated checkout before confirmed changes; resolve conflicting edits before execution.
- Preserve occupied layer, tag, and sorting-layer slots, existing quality entries, and assigned
  pipeline assets. Report a policy conflict instead of migrating outside the user's scope.
- Treat Preferences (Auto Refresh, worker count, script-change behavior) as machine-local; recommend,
  never change another person's workstation.
- Mark any check you cannot run **Not verified**.

## Review, recommend, confirm

This document always runs in four stages. Nothing is written to the project until stage 4 ends in an
explicit yes.

1. **Audit.** Read the project and report what already matches this document, what differs, and what
   could not be checked. Read-only.
2. **Recommend.** List every difference as a numbered recommendation: ID, finding, proposed change,
   why it matters, risk (low, medium, high), and a default (do or skip). List items that already
   match as "no change needed". Add recommendations of your own from what you found, including ones
   this document does not mention.
3. **Choose.** The user picks any subset of IDs, "all recommended", or none. Carry over only the
   picked items; unpicked items stay proposals in the report.
4. **Confirm.** Restate the exact changes for the picked subset (files, settings, values, commands)
   and wait for an explicit yes. Make no change before it, including saving the report. In a
   non-interactive session, or when no answer arrives, stop after stage 2 and change nothing.

Steps below that apply, install, or build run only after stage 4, and only for confirmed items. A new
finding during those steps becomes a new recommendation and returns to stage 3.

## 1. Preflight

Record (this is the audit input), in one table (setting, current value):

- Editor version from `ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt`. This document targets Unity 6 (6000.x).
  On an older Editor, report mismatches and apply nothing.
- Render pipeline, the URP package version, and the installed Input System package.
- The current value of every row in step 3, and the Enter Play Mode setting in Project Settings >
  Editor > Enter Play Mode Settings > **When entering Play Mode**.
- Source-control state, and whether the Editor is open.
- Mutable static state and static events in owned code (include mutable contents of `static readonly`
  collections as well as assignable fields; immutable constants and cached hashes need no reset), for the reload decision below. For a deeper,
  evidence-based audit, use the "Session reset" check of the
  [Scenes and lifecycle lens](../ProjectAuditGuides/UnityScenesAndLifecycleInstructions.md).

**Done:** the table exists, every row has a known value, an observed "not set", or Not verified with a reason,
and nothing was changed.

## 2. Ask

Ask in one batch. When the user says "use defaults", the default becomes a recommended answer that
still goes through stages 2 to 4.

| Question | Default |
|---|---|
| Stop after the recommendations, or choose items to apply? | Stop after the recommendations; the user chooses in stage 3 |
| Which input system, and which render pipeline? | Input System package and URP, unless the project already uses another |
| Reload policy (see the next section) | Keep the observed setting while auditing; for a new project, consider that Editor's default after reviewing static state |
| Source control in use? | Git, with visible meta files |
| Which platforms ship? | Ask; the build guides own platform settings |

**Done:** the mode and choices are repeated back, one line each.

## 3. Review and apply

Apply only the items confirmed in stage 4; every other row is reported. Mark each row **OK**,
**Differs** (report, and fix only if confirmed), **Not set** (observed absent), or **Not verified**
(value/evidence unavailable). An unknown value is neither an unset value nor a policy difference.

| Setting | Target | Read / set via | Condition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Asset Serialization Mode | Force Text | `EditorSettings.serializationMode` | Unity 6.7's default; makes diffs and merges readable |
| Version Control Mode | Visible Meta Files | `VersionControlSettings.mode` | Unity 6.7's default. Commit every `.meta` with its asset |
| Source control hygiene | `Library/`, `Temp/`, `Obj/`, `Logs/`, `UserSettings/` ignored; `Assets`, `Packages/manifest.json`, `Packages/packages-lock.json`, `ProjectSettings` committed | `.gitignore` ([version control guide](../VersionControl/README.md)) | Do not ignore `.meta` files |
| Input handling | Input System Package (New) | `Active Input Handling` in Player Settings; no public property, so use `SerializedObject` on `ProjectSettings.asset` or the window | Changing it needs an Editor restart. Unity documents the legacy Input Manager as deprecated. Choose Both only for a project mid-migration |
| API Compatibility Level | .NET Standard 2.1 | `PlayerSettings.SetApiCompatibilityLevel(NamedBuildTarget, …)` | .NET Framework only when a dependency requires it. Unity 6.7 also lists a CoreCLR (Experimental) scripting backend; do not select it as a baseline |
| Render pipeline | URP asset assigned as the default and in every quality level | `GraphicsSettings.defaultRenderPipeline`, `QualitySettings.renderPipeline` per level | URP 17.7 ships with 6.7; the Built-in pipeline is deprecated. Keep a working HDRP or Built-in project as it is |
| Color space | Linear | `PlayerSettings.colorSpace` | Gamma only for a deliberate legacy-device target |
| Enter Play Mode | See "Reload policy" | `EditorSettings.enterPlayModeOptionsEnabled`, `enterPlayModeOptions` | Verify against the dropdown after setting |
| Burst and jobs | Use through the installed API | Read the resolved package list | **6.6+:** Unity reports Burst as a built-in module with no package install. Earlier: `com.unity.burst`. Do not assume; read the resolved list |
| Batching | Rely on the SRP Batcher | Pipeline settings | **6.6+:** dynamic batching is obsolete |
| Compile-time symbols | Avoid `UNITY_64` and `DEVELOPMENT_BUILD` in new code | Search owned code | **6.6+:** both are deprecated, replaced by the Managed Code Variant setting; removal is planned for 6.8 |
| Packages | Manifest and lockfile committed; selected packages only | Package Manager Client API | Read the completed resolved list; never float versions |
| Tags, layers, sorting layers | Add only names the game uses | `TagManager` through `SerializedObject` | Never reuse or renumber an occupied slot |
| Scenes in the build | Only real scenes, enabled | `EditorBuildSettings.scenes` or Build Profiles | |
| Product and company name | Final values before any shipping build | `PlayerSettings.productName`, `companyName` | They set `persistentDataPath`; see the build guides |

Platform architecture, graphics APIs, scripting backend, stripping, and quality tiers belong to the
build guides ([desktop](../BuildSettings/DesktopBuilds.md), [mobile](../BuildSettings/MobileBuilds.md)).
Do not duplicate them here.

### Reload policy

**What changed.** Unity's 6.7 manual says the Editor does not reload the scripting domain on
entering Play mode by default, and recommends leaving it off for iteration speed and to prepare for
the CoreCLR runtime, which has no domain reload. The 6.6 release notes say the **new-project** default
changed from **Reload Domain and Scene** to **Reload Scene only**. Whether an *existing* project
keeps its old saved value is not stated, so read the actual setting.

**The dropdown** (Project Settings > Editor > Enter Play Mode Settings > **When entering Play
Mode**): Reload Domain and Scene · **Reload Scene only (the default)** · Reload Domain only ·
Do not reload Domain or Scene. Scripts set it with `EditorSettings.enterPlayModeOptionsEnabled` and
the `EnterPlayModeOptions` flags (`DisableDomainReload`, `DisableSceneReload`, `None`); the manual does
not map the dropdown to those flags, so set it, then read the dropdown back.

**What domain reload off means.** Static fields keep their values between Play sessions, static
events keep their subscribers, and non-serialized fields keep values from the last session. State
must be reset in code.

**The policy**

1. For a new project on 6.6+, **Reload Scene only** is the documented starting default: domain
   reload off, scene reload on. For an existing project or older Unity 6 Editor, retain the observed
   saved policy during audit; propose a change only after evaluating reset behavior for that version.
   Scene reload off changes teardown/restoration behavior and requires a deliberate project contract.
2. Audit mutable statics and static events (step 1, or the lens above for a full audit). In Unity 6.5+ (the attribute is documented from 6.5), mark each with
   `[AutoStaticsCleanup]` (events, delegates, collections of user objects, Unity object references)
   or `[NoAutoStaticsCleanup]` only for intentional cross-session persistence (for example unique-ID
   generators or safe cached UI resources), from `Unity.Scripting.LifecycleManagement`. The latter
   opts out of reset; session counters still need resetting. Types containing auto-cleaned fields
   must be `partial` (including containing types when required by the installed generator). Verify
   code generation and analyzer configuration; the analyzer reports `UAL0010` to `UAL0014`. For
   assignable fields the generator re-evaluates the initializer; supported `readonly` collections
   retain their instance and are cleared. Static constructors are not rerun.
3. Code that runs in Edit mode must reset on entering Play mode, because exit-time cleanup cannot be
   relied on there. On Editors before 6.5, reset with a `[RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod(
   RuntimeInitializeLoadType.SubsystemRegistration)]` method and unsubscribe static handlers.
4. If the audit finds many unprotected statics, set **Reload Domain and Scene** as a stopgap and
   record the follow-up. Say so in the report; do not leave it silent.

**Verify.** Press Play twice with a static counter and a static event subscriber: the second run
starts from the initial state, with no duplicate handler calls.

**Done:** the audit and numbered recommendations were shown and the user's explicit yes was received
before any change; every row has a status, the reload policy is recorded with the audit result, and
re-reading the settings returns the target values.

## 4. Optional choices

Offer these as recommendations; apply one only if it is picked and confirmed:

| Option | Choose when | Check |
|---|---|---|
| Reload Domain and Scene | Legacy code depends on a full reset | Two Plays are clean; accept the slower enter-Play time |
| Disable scene reload | The project deliberately restores object state | Repeated Plays and enable/disable tests pass |
| asmdefs | A concrete compile, dependency, or test boundary exists | Editor and player compile; tests are discovered in isolated assemblies |
| Quality tiers and volumes | Target hardware needs distinct budgets | Each tier runs on a representative device |
| Project Auditor | A broader review is wanted | Install `com.unity.project-auditor` through Package Manager; what it checks is not verified here |

## 5. Verify

- Read back every changed value. Reopen a scene and a prefab to confirm saved references survive.
- The project compiles in the Editor, and the project's tests pass.
- Press Play twice and confirm the reload contract above.
- An agreed platform build completes; otherwise mark it Not verified.

**Done:** each check is Passed, Failed, or Not verified.

## 6. Report

| Item | Status | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| Each step 3 row | OK / Differs / Applied / Not set / Not verified | Old value → new value |
| Reload policy | Kept / Stopgap | Audit result and follow-up |
| Each unpicked recommendation | Proposal | Finding, proposed change, and risk |
| Each step 5 check | Passed / Failed / Not verified | Evidence |

Put decisions you need, unpicked recommendations, conflicts, and failed checks in a "Needs your
decision" block at the top.

## References

- [Configuring how Unity enters Play mode](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/configurable-enter-play-mode.html)
- [Enter Play mode without domain reload](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/domain-reloading.html)
- [What's new in Unity 6.6](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/WhatsNewUnity66.html)
- [Upgrade to Unity 6.6](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/UpgradeGuideUnity66.html)
- [Editor settings reference](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/class-EditorManager.html)
- [EditorSettings.enterPlayModeOptions](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/EditorSettings-enterPlayModeOptions.html)
- [Input System installation](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.inputsystem@latest/index.html?subfolder=/manual/Installation.html)

Links follow current documentation; select the installed Editor/package version before applying an API or default.

# Set up a Unity project

Use this workflow for a new project or an explicitly scoped configuration change. It specifies
outcomes; available `new-unity-project`, `unity-cli`, and `unity-package-management` skills own
execution. This repository ships no automatic installer. Prefer Unity CLI; the Editor UI is the
fallback when CLI execution is unavailable.

This is a coordinator workflow: load the selected topic guides from the same source revision during
audit, then aggregate their recommendations below. If a delegated guide is unavailable, mark that
topic Not verified and continue independent work; do not claim the complete cross-topic audit ran.
The selected guides supply their own procedures, rather than duplicating them in this router.

For a single resource task, use its URL/local-file entry point and stop within that scope:

| Task | Entry point |
|---|---|
| Folders only | [Folder workflow](../FolderStructure/SetupFolders.md) |
| Git ignore, attributes, LFS, and merge setup | [Version control workflow](../VersionControl/SetupVersionControl.md) |
| CI checks and test gate | [CI workflow](../ContinuousIntegration/SetupCI.md) |
| Selected script templates | [Template workflow](../ScriptTemplates/SetupScriptTemplates.md) |
| Selected presets | [Preset workflow](../Presets/SetupPresets.md) |
| Update an existing kit installation | [Update workflow](../KitMaintenance/UpdateKit.md) |

These workflows use available tools without installing a project package or CLI. Template/preset
installation follows the [shared resource protocol](InstallResources.md); broader configuration below
remains a separate selection.

## Review, recommend, confirm

This document always runs in four stages. Nothing is written to the project until stage 4 ends in an
explicit yes.

1. **Audit.** Read the project and report what already matches this document, what differs, and what
   could not be checked. Read-only.
2. **Recommend.** List every difference as a numbered recommendation: ID, finding, proposed change,
   why it matters, risk (low, medium, high), and a default (do or skip). List items that already
   match as "no change needed". Add recommendations of your own from what you found, including ones
   this document does not mention.
3. **Choose.** The user picks any subset of IDs, "all recommended", or none. Carry over only the
   picked items; unpicked items stay proposals in the report.
4. **Confirm.** Restate the exact changes for the picked subset (files, settings, values, commands)
   and wait for an explicit yes. Make no change before it, including saving the report. In a
   non-interactive session, or when no answer arrives, stop after stage 2 and change nothing.

Steps below that apply, install, or build run only after stage 4, and only for confirmed items. A new
finding during those steps becomes a new recommendation and returns to stage 3.

**Across topics.** Each workflow this document delegates to (folders, version control, CI, script
templates, presets, and the guides in step 3) has its own review contract. Run their audit and
recommend stages first and aggregate every recommendation into one list, with IDs prefixed by topic,
so the user picks across topics once and confirms once. A delegated workflow must not re-prompt for
an item already confirmed here; it applies only the confirmed items from its own recommendations.

## 1. Establish choices

Confirm the destination, project name/namespace, installed Editor, platform, and selected resources.
Read [UnityTechStack.md](../../AgentsInstructions/UnityTechStack/UnityTechStack.md). Retain the URP/Input System/UI Toolkit/Awaitable/ObjectPool
profile unless the user selects another stack. The intended engine line is recorded there; use an
exact chosen release, not an assumed latest version. For an existing project, inspect its settings,
packages, dirty scenes, and source-control state first.

**Done:** selected choices and existing content are known; unresolved decisions affecting setup are
resolved. Avoid a general architecture interview for a small project.

## 2. Select and copy resources

Use [the installation guidance](../../README.md#how-to-install) and [snapshot manifest](installation.json)
for destinations. Preserve the reference hierarchy at `Documentation/UnityStarterKit/` outside `Assets`;
merge root instruction links with that prefix. Install only selected asset groups inside `Assets`. Preserve existing imported metadata
when copying the shipped resources. Do not overwrite the destination's instructions/configuration
without inspecting and merging them. Include the MIT license with reused resources.

**Done:** the reference snapshot and merged root instructions have resolving file links/anchors; `.editorconfig` is at the target root; only
selected presets/templates/examples are staged for import.

## 3. Configure the selected baseline

| Guide | Outcome | Selection |
|---|---|---|
| [Tech stack](../../AgentsInstructions/UnityTechStack/UnityTechStack.md) | Exact Editor/packages, selected systems, targets | Baseline |
| [Project settings](../ProjectSettings/README.md) | Settings match the agreed project/platform | Baseline plus explicit options |
| [Mac and Windows builds](../BuildSettings/DesktopBuilds.md) | Desktop support contract, budgets, build profiles, and native player acceptance | Only selected desktop targets |
| [Android and iOS builds](../BuildSettings/MobileBuilds.md) | Mobile support contract, store/toolchain checks, budgets, and device acceptance | Only selected mobile targets |
| [Package audit](../PackageInstaller/InstallPackages.md) | Existing dependencies inspected; only confirmed missing packages installed | When package setup or a missing prerequisite is in scope |
| [Folder layout](../FolderStructure/README.md) | Small owned feature layout and correct special folders | Baseline; expand when used |
| [Version control](../VersionControl/README.md) | Unity ignore and attribute rules installed; settings that Git depends on confirmed | Baseline |
| [CI](../ContinuousIntegration/README.md) | Licence-free checks installed; Editor tests run locally or on the user's own runner | When tests/examples selected |
| [Presets](../Presets/README.md) | Scoped import policy registered with tested filters | Optional assets |
| [Script templates](../ScriptTemplates/README.md) | Selected menu templates compile under their prerequisites | Optional assets |
| [Scene templates](../SceneTemplates/README.md) | Strategy sandbox, UI preview, and asset lookdev scenes with explicit dependency cloning | Optional assets |
| [Testing](../Testing/TestingInstructions.md) | Tests discoverable and excluded from normal players | When tests/examples selected |

Use CLI discovery rather than copying remembered commands:

```bash
unity --version
unity editors --installed --format json
unity templates list --help
unity status --format json
unity command --project-path /absolute/target/project --format json
```

Creation, Editor/module installation, package operations, and saved settings changes follow the
matching skills. For packages, invoke `UnityEditor.PackageManager.Client` through a supported CLI
command or batch Editor script; verify completed requests. Merely editing a dependency list is not
proof of resolution. Without CLI access, create the project in Hub, use Package Manager, and apply
settings in the Editor; mark unavailable automation checks explicitly.

**Done:** selected settings are read back, requested packages have resolved, and excluded options
have not been applied. Desktop tiers are selected through the desktop guide; fixed gameplay tags and networking are not assumed.

## 4. Import, save, and verify

Use Unity CLI to import and compile the target, then save selected assets/scenes through Editor APIs.
Inspect logs for compilation and UXML/USS/import warnings. Verify metadata and saved references,
restart/reopen the selected scene, and exercise repeated Play with the chosen reload settings.
Run selected tests through `unity test`; inspect fresh result XML. Build the agreed platform through
`unity build` or a CLI-invoked BuildPipeline script. Preserve unrelated dirty scenes.

**Done:** imported resources work from saved state; selected checks have results. An unavailable
Editor/device/build module leaves that check Not verified rather than silently passing.

## 5. Record the result

Update the target's tech-stack record with exact resolved versions, platform/backend, reload choice,
and deviations. Report changed resources/settings, validation results, and remaining limitations.
Record source revision, destinations, selected groups and local adaptations in
`Documentation/UnityStarterKit-installation.json` when selected, so a future update has a baseline.

**Done:** selected choices, evidence, and deviations are recorded or reported with unavailable checks explicit.

Commit only within the user's source-control scope; inspect generated-folder exclusions first.
[Validation.md](../../Validation.md) records testing of this starter, not every downstream project.

## Optional migration

[CoreCLRUpgrade.md](../CoreCLRmigration/CoreCLRUpgrade.md) is a dated compatibility reference. Load only for an actual
migration; it is not a required step for creating the selected baseline.

> How it works: give this URL to your agent, for example "Set up folders only in my Unity project
> from this document". The agent audits the project, recommends the folders that fit, lets you pick
> which to carry over, and creates nothing until you confirm the exact list. Then it reports what it
> verified. Human overview: [readme](README.md).

# Set up project folders (agent instructions)

Scaffold the owned-content folders of a newly created Unity project. This document is
self-contained and creates directories only: presets, script templates, scenes, asmdefs, packages,
project settings, and copied guides are separate tasks. Use the tools you already have; install
no package, CLI, or setup script. **Last verified: October 2026.**

## Operating rules

- Create the selected missing directories and nothing else. Never generate `.meta` files, move,
  rename, or delete existing content, or create suffixed duplicates to dodge a conflict.
- The target project's own instructions take precedence over this document.
- Leave existing assets, instructions, and unsaved work untouched.
- When required instructions cannot be read, stop before creating anything rather than working
  from memory. Report the source URL or path you followed.
- Report folder creation and Unity import verification as two separate results.

## Review, recommend, confirm

This document always runs in four stages. Nothing is written to the project until stage 4 ends in an
explicit yes.

1. **Audit.** Read the project and report what already matches this document, what differs, and what
   could not be checked. Read-only.
2. **Recommend.** List every difference as a numbered recommendation: ID, finding, proposed change,
   why it matters, risk (low, medium, high), and a default (do or skip). List items that already
   match as "no change needed". Add recommendations of your own from what you found, including ones
   this document does not mention.
3. **Choose.** The user picks any subset of IDs, "all recommended", or none. Carry over only the
   picked items; unpicked items stay proposals in the report.
4. **Confirm.** Restate the exact changes for the picked subset (files, settings, values, commands)
   and wait for an explicit yes. Make no change before it, including saving the report. In a
   non-interactive session, or when no answer arrives, stop after stage 2 and change nothing.

Steps below that apply, install, or build run only after stage 4, and only for confirmed items. A new
finding during those steps becomes a new recommendation and returns to stage 3.

## 1. Preflight

Identify the target: the user's destination, or the current workspace when it is exactly one Unity
project (it contains `Assets` and `ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt`). Resolve an ambiguous
destination before writing. This starter repository is not a Unity project.

Inspect the existing folders under `Assets`, any established owned-content root, source-control
changes when available, and whether the project's Editor is open.

Look for what the Unity template left behind. Template-created projects arrive with a
`Assets/Settings` folder (its contents depend on the template, for example render pipeline and volume
settings) and often a sample scene and sample assets. List what exists by inspection, and do not
assume names. Reuse `Assets/Settings` as it stands; leave sample content in place and report it.

Check the project's location. The full path and project name should contain no spaces, and the
project should sit close to the drive root on Windows: [reported path-length failures](https://discussions.unity.com/t/unity-editor-still-hits-windows-max-path-260-char-limit-even-with-longpathsenabled-any-real-fix/1732098)
hit IL2CPP and Android builds, and Unity publishes no safe limit. Warn the user when the path is long
instead of moving the project.

**Done:** the target project, local rules, existing folders, template leftovers, path length, and
Editor state are known, and nothing has been created.

## 2. Ask

Ask only what changes the result, in one short round. The defaults are recommended answers: they
become recommendations that still go through stages 3 and 4, even when the user says "use defaults".

| Question | Default |
|---|---|
| Owned-content root name? | An existing root if one is established; otherwise `Assets/{ProjectName}`, using the project directory's name |
| Which real features exist now, and what does each need next? | None: create the root alone |
| Project-wide `Scenes`, `Settings`, or `Shared`? | Only for a responsibility the user selects |
| `Tests/EditMode` and `Tests/PlayMode` folders? | No |
| `Resources`, `Plugins`, or `StreamingAssets`? | No: create only for an actual loading, plugin, or raw-content requirement |
| Extra feature subfolders (`Audio`, `Animations`, `VFX`, `Materials`)? | None: add per feature when content of that kind exists |
| Keep source art files (PSD, Blend, and similar) in the project? | No. When yes, use a project-root `ArtSource` folder beside `Assets`, outside the import pipeline |
| Reusable code to share across projects? | No. A local package is a separate task, not part of folder scaffolding |
| Sample content from the template? | Leave it in place and report it |

**Done:** every proposed directory has a stated purpose and a concrete path under the target `Assets`,
or is the explicitly selected project-root `ArtSource` beside `Assets`.

## 3. Choose the layout

Use this tree as a menu. Each branch that fits the project becomes a numbered recommendation, with
its purpose and risk; `Inventory` and its UI files are an example feature, not scaffolding to copy.

```text
ArtSource/                # Optional, beside Assets: PSD, Blend, and other source files Unity should not import
Packages/                 # Unity-managed; embedded packages live here (separate task)
Assets/
├── ScriptTemplates/      # Selected .cs.txt files (separate task); must be a direct child of Assets
├── StreamingAssets/      # Optional raw player content; must be a direct child of Assets
├── ThirdPartyAssets/     # Vendor imports whose layout permits relocation
├── Settings/Presets/     # Selected import presets (separate task); a starter convention, not a Unity special folder
└── {ProjectName}/
    ├── SceneTemplates/   # Optional source scenes/templates and shared resources
    ├── Scenes/           # Bootstrap, composition, and other project-wide scenes
    ├── Settings/         # Project-wide URP, Input Actions, shared UI settings
    ├── Shared/           # Independent shared code and content
    └── Inventory/        # Example feature; create the real ones
        ├── Scenes/       # Optional feature-owned, test, or demo scenes
        ├── Scripts/
        ├── Editor/
        ├── Tests/        # Optional; EditMode/ and PlayMode/ subfolders
        ├── Data/         # Authored configuration assets
        ├── Prefabs/
        ├── Art/          # Models, textures, materials; add Audio/, Animations/, VFX/ when used
        └── UI/           # UXML, USS, and C# for a screen together; Sprites/ for UI sprites
```

Name every folder you create in PascalCase, with no spaces and consistent casing. Do not start a
name with a dot: the Editor's create menu turns a leading dot into an underscore, and Unity ignores
dot-prefixed folders when importing. Unity also ignores folders ending in `~` and folders named
`cvs`, so use that suffix only when you intend the contents to stay out of the project (for example
`Documentation~`). Keep nesting shallow: aim for at most four levels below the owned-content root.
Those naming and nesting limits are this guide's recommendations, not Unity requirements.

Apply these ownership rules when placing a folder:

- Put code, configuration, and content with the feature that owns its meaning, even when another
  feature consumes it. Multiple consumers alone do not make something shared.
- Use `Shared` only for content with an independent responsibility that depends on no feature
  implementation, through code or asset references.
- Use project-level `Scenes` and `Settings` for composition and configuration that spans features.
- Keep guides, build outputs, and validation reports outside `Assets`.
- Create `Resources` or `Plugins` only for an actual loading or plugin requirement, and honor
  platform-specific plugin paths. Custom Android Gradle templates and a custom main manifest
  belong in `Assets/Plugins/Android/`; Unity generates them when the matching Publishing Settings
  option is enabled, so enable the option instead of creating the files by hand. See the
  [mobile build setup](../BuildSettings/MobileBuilds.md).
- Keep reusable cross-project code out of `Shared`. Unity's custom-package layout (a folder with a
  `package.json`, plus `Runtime`, `Editor`, and `Tests`) in `Packages/` is the supported home for it;
  do not create `package.json` files in this workflow.
- Keep source art in `ArtSource`, beside `Assets`, instead of importing it.
- Defer `Assets/Settings/Presets` and `Assets/ScriptTemplates` to their own workflows.
- Folder creation does not configure test assemblies or asmdefs, and it does not create placeholder
  files or a permanent setup report to keep empty folders alive.

**Done:** the recommended project-relative paths are listed and shown to the user, who has picked a
subset and confirmed it in stage 4. Stop to ask about unresolved choices or conflicts.

## 4. Check, then create

Only the items confirmed in stage 4 are created. Check the complete confirmed path list before
changing anything:

- Each name is a valid single directory segment on the target platform. Reject absolute names,
  separators, `.` and `..`, and case-only collisions with selected or existing paths.
- Every destination resolves inside the intended project's `Assets`, or is the selected project-root
  `ArtSource`. Do not create through a symlinked entry inside `Assets`.
- Reuse an existing directory with matching name and casing. A file at a requested directory path,
  or metadata for a missing directory, is a conflict to resolve before creating anything.

Choose the route by destination, scope, and Editor state:

- **Project-root ArtSource only:** after exact confirmation, create the selected missing directory
  with ordinary filesystem operations. It stays outside Unity import regardless of Editor state.
- **New-project Assets scaffolding, Editor closed:** create only the selected missing directories
  with ordinary filesystem operations. Unity generates their metadata on import.
- **Editor open:** use existing Editor access (for example an `AssetDatabase` folder API) for selected
  imported folders, checking each path first and targeting the project explicitly. If unavailable,
  defer creation or ask for a safe closed-Editor route for new-project scaffolding. Never install a
  bridge or close an Editor with unsaved work.
- **Established project Assets changes:** continue read-only inventory, then route imported-folder
  additions or reorganization to [ReviewFolders.md](ReviewFolders.md) for an Editor-owned plan.
  An existing owned root alone does not imply reorganization, and does not block a specifically
  selected project-root ArtSource proposal. This workflow never moves existing content.

If a failure interrupts creation, report the paths already created. A rerun must reuse them and
create only the remaining selected directories.

**Done:** the audit and recommendation list were shown and confirmed before any change, and each
confirmed path is Created or Already present, with existing content and metadata unchanged.

## 5. Verify

- Read back every selected path and confirm it is a directory with the intended casing.
- Repeat the missing-folder check; it must find nothing to create.
- Compare before and after. Only the selected directories and Unity-generated folder metadata belong
  to this run. Preserve unrelated concurrent edits.
- After an observed Unity import, confirm that the new folders under `Assets` have generated
  metadata (folders ending in `~` and `ArtSource` get none, by design), GUIDs are unique, pre-existing metadata is unchanged, and the import log has no fresh errors. Open the project
  for import only when a safe route exists and doing so is within scope; otherwise mark the import
  checks **Not verified** and tell the user to open the project in Unity.
- Run no gameplay tests or player build for empty-folder scaffolding.

Empty directories may not survive source control. Commit Unity-generated metadata together with the
folders once it exists.

**Done:** directory verification passes, a repeat run has nothing to add, and the import result is
Verified or Not verified.

## 6. Report

| Item | Status | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| Target project, content root, source URL | | |
| Audit and recommendations shown, confirmation received | Yes / Stopped before confirming | Items picked |
| Unpicked recommendations | Proposal | Path and reason |
| Template leftovers (`Assets/Settings`, sample content) | Reused / Left in place | What exists |
| Project path | OK / Warned | Length and spaces |
| Each selected path | Created / Already present / Conflict | Path |
| Missing-folder recheck | Passed / Failed | |
| Unity import and metadata | Verified / Not verified | Next action if pending |

Put unresolved conflicts, unpicked recommendations that need a ruling, and open choices in a
"Needs your decision" block at the top.

## References

- [Special folder names](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/SpecialFolders.html)
- [Default project directories](https://docs.unity.com/en-us/engine/6000.6/manual/get-started/project-configuration/default-directories)
- [Custom package layout](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/cus-layout.html)
- [Organizing your Unity project](https://unity.com/how-to/organizing-your-project)
- [Assembly definitions](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/assembly-definitions-intro.html)
- [StreamingAssets](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/StreamingAssets.html)
