# Mac and Windows desktop build setup (agent instructions)

Configure the Windows and macOS standalone players of a URP project on Unity 6.7+. This document is
self-contained. Its values are starting choices: keep a setting that already works unless the user
selects the change, and treat every budget as a proposal until measured on a device.
**Last verified: October 2026** (Unity 6.7 docs era); re-check deprecations and store rules after that.

## Operating rules

- Change settings through Editor APIs or Unity CLI (`PlayerSettings`, `QualitySettings`,
  `EditorUserBuildSettings`, Build Profile assets). Leave ProjectSettings YAML and `.meta` files
  untouched; hand edits corrupt asset identity.
- Continue read-only auditing on a dirty tree while preserving existing edits and unsaved scenes.
  Before confirmed changes, establish an attributable before/after baseline or an isolated checkout.
  Ask before execution only when existing work conflicts with it; a dirty tree alone does not gate the audit.
- Preserve unsaved scenes and the user's other edits.
- Without CLI/bridge access, inspect saved files read-only and mark unavailable live checks Not verified.
  After confirmation, use the Editor's Player Settings, Quality, and Build Profiles windows and
  importer Inspectors as the manual route; install no bridge merely to complete this guide.
- Confirm each API signature against the installed Editor version before calling it; the names
  below are the Unity 6 shape and move between releases.
- Record a check as **Not verified** when its module, host OS, or device is missing. A build that
  succeeds on one platform proves nothing about another.

## Review, recommend, confirm

This document always runs in four stages. Nothing is written to the project until stage 4 ends in an
explicit user confirmation.

1. **Audit.** Read the project and report what already matches this document, what differs, and what
   could not be checked. Read-only.
2. **Recommend.** List every difference as a numbered recommendation: ID, finding, proposed change,
   why it matters, risk (low, medium, high), and a default (do or skip). List items that already
   match as "no change needed". Add recommendations of your own from what you found, including ones
   this document does not mention.
3. **Choose.** The user picks any subset of IDs, "all recommended", or none. Carry over only the
   picked items; unpicked items stay proposals in the report.
4. **Confirm.** Present the exact changes for the picked subset (files, settings, values, commands)
   and obtain explicit user authorization before making them, including saving the report.
   Confirmation need not contain the literal word "yes": after the concrete scope is presented,
   "implement R1 and R3" can both select and confirm those items. Selection alone ("R1 and R3")
   chooses scope without authorizing implementation. Honor existing authorization for unchanged
   scope without asking again; clarify a delayed reply only when its scope is materially ambiguous.
   Changed scope needs confirmation for the changed items. In a non-interactive session, or when
   authorization is absent, stop after stage 2 and change nothing.

Steps below that apply, install, or build run only after stage 4, and only for confirmed items. A new
finding during those steps becomes a new recommendation and returns to stage 3.

## 1. Preflight

Read (this is the audit), then summarise in one table (setting, current value):

- Editor version (`ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt`) and installed Windows/macOS build modules.
- Render pipeline and the URP asset assigned to every quality level; installed Input System package.
- Current values of every row in step 3, plus existing Build Profiles and scripting define symbols.
- Host OS. macOS builds need a Mac. A Windows IL2CPP build needs Visual Studio with the C++ tools
  component and a Windows SDK at or above the minimum in the
  [Windows requirements](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/windows-requirements-and-compatibility.html);
  a Mac IL2CPP build needs Xcode.

**Done:** the table exists, every step 3 row has a known value, an observed "not set", or Not verified with a reason,
and nothing was changed.

## 2. Ask the support contract

Ask all questions in one batch; the project cannot answer them. When the user says "use defaults",
the default becomes a recommended answer that still goes through stages 2 to 4.

| Question | Default |
|---|---|
| Which targets ship? | Windows x64 and macOS Apple Silicon |
| Support Windows Arm64? | No. It has no Vulkan, only GPU lightmapping, and needs Arm64 builds of every native dependency |
| Support Intel Macs? | No. Unity deprecates Intel Mac from 6.6; Intel or Universal output is possible only on Unity 6.7 LTS or earlier |
| Minimum Windows/macOS release, GPU, CPU, RAM? | No default; record unanswered values as "unspecified" |
| Need D3D12-only features (for example ray tracing)? | No: D3D11 baseline |
| Frame budget? | 60 fps (16.7 ms) on the minimum device |
| Delivery channel (Steam, store, direct download)? | Direct download |
| Run builds now? | Yes when the host and modules exist; otherwise configure only |

**Done:** every question has an answer or a stated default, repeated back to the user, one line each.

## 3. Apply the settings

Only the items confirmed in stage 4. Go row by row. When a row's current value already matches its
target, record **Already correct**; a row the user did not pick is **Skipped** and stays a proposal.

| Setting | Target | Set via | Condition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Company and Product name | Final names, set before any shipping build | `PlayerSettings.companyName`, `productName` | They determine `persistentDataPath` and the Player.log path, so a later rename moves player data |
| Color space | Linear | `PlayerSettings.colorSpace` | |
| Render pipeline | URP asset assigned in every quality level | `QualitySettings.renderPipeline` per level | |
| Windows graphics APIs | D3D11 first; Auto Graphics API off when the order is manual | `PlayerSettings.SetUseDefaultGraphicsAPIs`, `SetGraphicsAPIs` | With D3D12 selected, keep D3D11 in the list: Unity [blocks D3D12 on some devices](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/allow-deny-d3d12-usage.html), and a build without a fallback does not launch there |
| Mac graphics API | Metal | same | |
| Mac architecture | Apple Silicon (`OSArchitecture.ARM64`) | `OSXStandalone.UserBuildSettings.architecture` | Intel only when selected in step 2 |
| Windows architecture | x64 | Build Profile or Player Settings architecture field; find the API for the installed Editor | Arm64 only when selected |
| Fullscreen mode | Fullscreen Window (borderless) | `PlayerSettings.fullScreenMode` | Offer Exclusive Fullscreen (Windows only) as a user option, never the default |
| Resizable window | On | `PlayerSettings.resizableWindow` | |
| Run in background | Off for an offline game; on only when online or background simulation requires it | `PlayerSettings.runInBackground` | |
| High DPI | Retina/high-DPI support on, plus a user render-scale option | `PlayerSettings.macRetinaSupport`; Windows per Player Settings | |
| vSync | 1 in every quality level | `QualitySettings.vSyncCount` | `Application.targetFrameRate` is ignored while vSync is above 0. With vSync off, offer a frame limiter; avoid an unlimited default on laptops |
| Scripting backend | Mono for development, IL2CPP for release | `PlayerSettings.SetScriptingBackend(NamedBuildTarget.Standalone, …)` | IL2CPP for both when a dependency requires it. IL2CPP is not faster by default; measure |
| Managed stripping | Minimal in both profiles | `PlayerSettings.SetManagedStrippingLevel` | Raise one level at a time, only after reflection, serialization, and dynamic-content tests pass on the release player |
| Input | Keep the project's active input handling; prefer the Input System package for new projects | Player Settings | |

### Quality tiers

Create Laptop and Desktop tiers (add High only when it serves a distinct device class). Each tier
gets its own URP asset and an explicit budget. Treat shadows, render scale, anti-aliasing,
additional lights, and post-processing as tier choices driven by GPU timing. Keep a renderer
feature that already works; enabling every feature is not a baseline.

### Texture and audio budgets (proposals)

Apply through `TextureImporter` platform settings on owned assets only, after previewing the paths.
The Standalone override is shared by Windows and macOS; split content when their budgets diverge.
Keep color textures sRGB and data textures linear.

| Role | Starting budget | Inspect before accepting |
|---|---|---|
| World albedo | Max 2048; BC7 for quality, BC1 for opaque | Compare at gameplay distance; small props 512–1024 |
| Normal maps | Max 2048; evaluate BC5 | Tangent-space shading and the shader's normal decoding |
| Packed masks | 1024–2048; BC7 when several channels are needed | Required channels, metallic/smoothness artifacts |
| Close-up hero surfaces | 4096 only where a comparison justifies it | Imported memory size and total residency |
| Screen-space UI | Match displayed size; compare BC7 with RGBA32 | Alpha edges at high DPI; keep slicing and atlas identity |

Audio: music and long ambience stream (Vorbis); short SFX decompress on load; keep sample rate
content-driven. Existing platform overrides take precedence and need their own audit.

### Shader and pipeline-state warm-up

First-use shader compilation causes desktop hitches. Use `GraphicsStateCollection` (experimental):
trace pipeline states in a test build, then warm the collection during a loading screen. It covers
D3D12, Vulkan, and Metal, and falls back to shader warm-up elsewhere. Re-trace after content
changes; OS and driver updates invalidate driver caches. See
[PSO tracing and warm-up](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/shader-pso-introduction.html).

**Done:** the audit and numbered recommendations were shown and the user's explicit confirmation was received
before any change; every row has a status (Applied, Already correct, or Skipped with reason), and
re-reading the settings through the Editor API returns the target values.

## 4. Build profiles and CLI

Only the items confirmed in stage 4. Create Development and Release profiles only for the selected
platforms (Windows and/or Mac) through the Editor or CLI. Unselected platforms need no profiles or hosts. Not every setting is isolated per profile in every Editor version, so inspect shared
Player Settings after saving.

| Choice | Development | Release |
|---|---|---|
| Development Build | On | Off |
| Script debugging / profiler | On only when needed; Deep Profiling off | Off |
| Backend | Mono (step 3) | IL2CPP (step 3), exercised in acceptance |
| Output | `Builds/<Platform>-<Profile>/`, outside `Assets` | Same; clean distributable |

Build from the CLI, one target per invocation (`-projectPath` and `-quit` are required;
`-batchmode` and `-logFile` are recommended):

```
Unity -batchmode -quit -projectPath <abs path> -activeBuildProfile <profile asset> -build <output path> -logFile <log>
```

Use `-buildTarget` when no profile asset exists, or `-executeMethod` for a custom build script.
Without either, Unity loads the last-used configuration. Prefer the installed `unity` CLI when
present and read its help for exact flags.

Preserve debug symbols separately. For Mac distribution, plan signing and notarization for the
chosen channel and test the result on another Mac. For Windows, record the code-signing and
packaging requirements of the chosen channel.

**Done:** each selected release profile builds on a suitable host, or its build is marked Not verified
with the missing prerequisite. Unselected platforms are Not applicable.

## 5. Verify

Run the project's tests and read fresh results. In the release player of each selected platform,
check:

- keyboard/mouse input and UI focus; controller input when the game supports controllers
- resize, fullscreen switching, Alt-Tab/Cmd-Tab, and saved display preferences
- Retina/high-DPI and an ordinary display, with UI inspected and GPU frame time noted
- 60 Hz, a high-refresh display, and on Mac a variable-refresh (ProMotion) display
- first audio playback and overlapping voices, scene transitions, save/load, quit and relaunch
- a cold shader cache (clear the driver cache) shows no first-use hitches in each scene
- the minimum quality tier on the minimum hardware, with frame time and memory recorded
- Player.log shows no missing shaders, assets, native libraries, or runtime types

Player.log: Windows `%USERPROFILE%\AppData\LocalLow\<Company>\<Product>\Player.log`; macOS
`~/Library/Logs/<Company>/<Product>/Player.log` ([log files](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/LogFiles.html)).

**Done:** each check is Passed, Failed, or Not verified, with resolution, API, refresh rate, and
hardware recorded beside every measurement.

## 6. Report

End with this table and a `git diff --stat ProjectSettings` summary:

| Item | Status | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| Each step 3 row | Applied / Already correct / Skipped | Old value → new value |
| Each unpicked recommendation | Proposal | Finding, proposed change, and risk |
| Each step 5 check | Passed / Failed / Not verified | Evidence, or the missing module, host, or device |

Put unanswered support-contract items, unpicked recommendations that need a decision, and failed
checks in a separate block labelled "Needs your decision" at the top of the report.

## References

- [Windows Player settings](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/playersettings-windows.html)
- [Windows requirements and compatibility](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/windows-requirements-and-compatibility.html)
- [macOS build settings and architectures](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/macosbuildsettings.html)
- [Intel Mac deprecation](https://discussions.unity.com/t/unity-to-deprecate-intel-based-mac-support-starting-with-unity-6-6/1721740)
- [D3D12 device filtering](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/allow-deny-d3d12-usage.html)
- [PSO tracing and warm-up](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/shader-pso-introduction.html)
- [vSync and frame limiting](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/QualitySettings-vSyncCount.html)
- [Build profiles](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/build-profiles.html)
- [Build from the command line](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/build-command-line.html)
- [Log files](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/LogFiles.html)

> How it works: give this URL to your agent, for example "Implement the mobile build settings from
> this document in my Unity project". The agent audits the project first, asks about your target
> devices and stores, recommends changes, lets you pick which to carry over, and changes nothing
> until you confirm. It then applies the confirmed settings and reports what it verified. Human
> overview: [readme](README.md).

# Android and iOS mobile build setup (agent instructions)

Configure the Android and iOS players of a URP project on Unity 6.7+. This document is
self-contained. Its values are starting choices: keep a setting that already works unless the user
selects the change, and treat every budget as a proposal until measured on a physical device.
**Last verified: October 2026.** Store rules change yearly, so re-check the linked Google Play and
Apple pages before a release.

## Operating rules

- Change settings through Editor APIs or Unity CLI (`PlayerSettings`, `QualitySettings`,
  `EditorUserBuildSettings`, Build Profile assets). Leave ProjectSettings YAML and `.meta` files
  untouched; hand edits corrupt asset identity.
- Continue read-only auditing on a dirty tree while preserving existing edits and unsaved scenes.
  Before confirmed changes, establish an attributable before/after baseline or an isolated checkout.
  Ask before execution only when existing work conflicts with it; a dirty tree alone does not gate the audit.
- Preserve unsaved scenes and the user's other edits.
- Without CLI/bridge access, inspect saved files read-only and mark unavailable live checks Not verified.
  After confirmation, use the Editor's Player Settings, Quality, and Build Profiles windows and
  importer Inspectors as the manual route; install no bridge merely to complete this guide.
- Keep signing material out of the project and out of the report: keystores, passwords, and
  provisioning profiles stay in the user's secure storage. Ask the user to supply them at build time.
- Confirm each API signature against the installed Editor version before calling it; the names
  below are the Unity 6 shape and move between releases.
- Record a check as **Not verified** when its module, host OS, or physical device is missing.
  Simulators and emulators do not establish performance, thermals, or driver behavior.

## Review, recommend, confirm

This document always runs in four stages. Nothing is written to the project until stage 4 ends in an
explicit user confirmation.

1. **Audit.** Read the project and report what already matches this document, what differs, and what
   could not be checked. Read-only.
2. **Recommend.** List every difference as a numbered recommendation: ID, finding, proposed change,
   why it matters, risk (low, medium, high), and a default (do or skip). List items that already
   match as "no change needed". Add recommendations of your own from what you found, including ones
   this document does not mention.
3. **Choose.** The user picks any subset of IDs, "all recommended", or none. Carry over only the
   picked items; unpicked items stay proposals in the report.
4. **Confirm.** Present the exact changes for the picked subset (files, settings, values, commands)
   and obtain explicit user authorization before making them, including saving the report.
   Confirmation need not contain the literal word "yes": after the concrete scope is presented,
   "implement R1 and R3" can both select and confirm those items. Selection alone ("R1 and R3")
   chooses scope without authorizing implementation. Honor existing authorization for unchanged
   scope without asking again; clarify a delayed reply only when its scope is materially ambiguous.
   Changed scope needs confirmation for the changed items. In a non-interactive session, or when
   authorization is absent, stop after stage 2 and change nothing.

Steps below that apply, install, or build run only after stage 4, and only for confirmed items. A new
finding during those steps becomes a new recommendation and returns to stage 3.

## 1. Preflight

Read (this is the audit), then summarise in one table (setting, current value):

- Editor version (`ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt`) and installed Android and iOS build modules.
- Render pipeline and the URP asset assigned to every quality level; installed Input System package.
- Current values of every row in step 3, plus existing Build Profiles and scripting define symbols.
- Host OS and toolchains. Android needs the SDK, NDK, and JDK that Unity Hub installs with the
  module. iOS builds need a Mac with Xcode: the Unity build produces an Xcode project, and
  Xcode compiles, signs, and archives it.

**Done:** the table exists, every step 3 row has a known value, an observed "not set", or Not verified with a reason,
and nothing was changed.

## 2. Ask the target contract

Ask all questions in one batch; the project cannot answer them. When the user says "use defaults",
the default becomes a recommended answer that still goes through stages 2 to 4.

| Question | Default |
|---|---|
| Which platforms ship? | Android and iOS |
| Store or distribution channel? | Google Play (App Bundle) and the App Store |
| Minimum Android API level and minimum iOS version? | No default; propose the Editor's current minimum and ask |
| Representative low-end device per platform? | No default; record "unspecified" and mark device checks Not verified |
| Orientation? | Keep the project's current setting; ask only when none is set |
| Frame-rate target? | 30 fps for a low tier, 60 fps for mid and high tiers |
| Need 32-bit Android (ARMv7)? | No: ARM64 only |
| Which permissions does the game use (camera, microphone, location, notifications)? | None; every unused permission stays out of the manifest and Info.plist |
| iOS build method: Replace or Append the Xcode project? | Replace for clean CI; Append when the user hand-edits the Xcode project |
| Run builds now? | Yes when toolchains and modules exist; otherwise configure only |

**Done:** every question has an answer or a stated default, repeated back to the user, one line each.

## 3. Apply the settings

Only the items confirmed in stage 4. Go row by row. When a row's current value already matches its
target, record **Already correct**; a row the user did not pick is **Skipped** and stays a proposal.

### Shared

| Setting | Target | Set via | Condition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Company and Product name, bundle identifier | Final values, set before any shipping build | `PlayerSettings.companyName`, `productName`, `SetApplicationIdentifier` | A later change breaks store identity and moves `persistentDataPath` |
| Version and build number | Set both; the build number increases with every store upload | `PlayerSettings.bundleVersion`, `Android.bundleVersionCode`, `iOS.buildNumber` | |
| Color space | Linear | `PlayerSettings.colorSpace` | Gamma only when the minimum device list requires it |
| Scripting backend | IL2CPP | `PlayerSettings.SetScriptingBackend(NamedBuildTarget.Android / .iOS, …)` | |
| Managed stripping | Minimal while iterating; raise one level at a time for release | `PlayerSettings.SetManagedStrippingLevel` | Only after reflection, serialization, and dynamic-content tests pass on the release player |
| Frame rate | `Application.targetFrameRate` = the user's target, set at startup; `QualitySettings.vSyncCount` = 0 | Code plus `QualitySettings` | Android and iOS ignore positive `vSyncCount` values and use `targetFrameRate`; setting vSync to 0 is not a prerequisite on these platforms. Test pacing and refresh-rate changes on devices |
| Incremental GC | On | `PlayerSettings.gcIncremental` | |
| Input | Input System package with touch support | Package Manager and Player Settings | |
| Safe area | Read `Screen.safeArea` and anchor HUD inside it | Code | Notches and rounded corners cut content on both platforms |

### Android

| Setting | Target | Set via | Condition |
|---|---|---|---|
| App icons | Adaptive icons only | Android Player Settings > Icons | Unity 6.6 removed Legacy and Round icon support |
| Target architectures | ARM64 only | `PlayerSettings.Android.targetArchitectures` | ARMv7 only when selected; Google Play requires 64-bit support alongside it |
| Target API level | At least API 36 (Android 16) | `PlayerSettings.Android.targetSdkVersion` | New apps and updates on Google Play need it from 31 August 2026 (extensions to 1 November 2026 exist). Existing apps need at least API 35. [Check the requirement](https://developer.android.com/google/play/requirements/target-sdk) before release |
| Minimum API level | The user's answer | `PlayerSettings.Android.minSdkVersion` | Never below the Editor's supported floor |
| Release output | Android App Bundle (`.aab`) | `EditorUserBuildSettings.buildAppBundle` = true | Google Play requires it; use `.apk` for development and side-loading |
| Graphics APIs | Vulkan first, OpenGL ES 3.1 as fallback | `PlayerSettings.SetGraphicsAPIs(BuildTarget.Android, …)` | Unity 6.6 raised the minimum OpenGL ES version from 3.0 to 3.1 (upgrade guide). Test both on the low-end device. Use Vulkan device filter lists when a driver misbehaves |
| Optimized Frame Pacing | On | `PlayerSettings.Android.optimizedFramePacing` | With it on, Unity can clamp `targetFrameRate` to a divisor of the refresh rate (for example 25 → 20 on 60 Hz); pick targets that divide 60 |
| Texture compression | ASTC | Player Settings Android texture compression | ETC2 only when the minimum device lacks ASTC |
| Application entry point | Keep the project's current entry; ship a single entry in store builds | Android Player Settings | |
| 16 KB page size | Every native library aligned for 16 KB pages | Unity 6 supports it; inspect the built bundle (APK Analyzer) | Play rejects apps targeting Android 15+ that fail it. If a rejection persists on a supported Editor, update the `com.unity.appbundle` package (it updates bundletool) |
| Signing | Release keystore from the user's secure storage; Play App Signing for the upload key | `PlayerSettings.Android.useCustomKeystore` and keystore fields, supplied at build time | |

### iOS

| Setting | Target | Set via | Condition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Architecture | ARM64 | Player Settings (Unity iOS builds are ARM64) | |
| Minimum iOS version | The user's answer | `PlayerSettings.iOS.targetOSVersionString` | Never below the Editor's supported floor |
| Target SDK | Device SDK for release; Simulator SDK only for simulator runs | `PlayerSettings.iOS.sdkVersion` | |
| Graphics API | Metal (leave Auto Graphics API on) | `PlayerSettings.SetUseDefaultGraphicsAPIs` | |
| Xcode and SDK | Build with Xcode 26 and the iOS 26 SDK or newer | Mac host | App Store Connect has required it for uploads since 28 April 2026; [check Apple's requirements](https://developer.apple.com/news/upcoming-requirements/) |
| Privacy manifest | `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy` declaring required-reason APIs; every third-party SDK ships its own | Xcode project / Unity privacy manifest policy | Missing declarations get uploads rejected. [Unity's policy](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/apple-privacy-manifest-policy.html) |
| Usage descriptions | A purpose string for each permission the game actually uses (step 2) | `PlayerSettings.iOS.cameraUsageDescription`, `microphoneUsageDescription`, `locationUsageDescription` | Leave unused strings empty |
| Signing | Apple Developer Team ID set; automatic signing for development, explicit provisioning for release | `PlayerSettings.iOS.appleDeveloperTeamID`, `appleEnableAutomaticSigning` | Certificates and profiles stay in the user's keychain |
| Output | Xcode project under `Builds/iOS/`, outside `Assets` | Build Profile / `BuildPlayerOptions` | Use the build method chosen in step 2 |

### Quality tiers and budgets (proposals)

Create Low, Mid, and High tiers, each with its own URP asset. Assign the tier from device
capability at startup, and give each tier a frame and memory budget. Start from these URP choices
and let GPU timing on the low-end device decide:

- HDR off and MSAA 0 or 2 on Low; shadows off or a single low-resolution cascade; at most a few
  additional lights; render scale below 1 on Low if the budget requires it.
- Post-processing minimal; leave the depth texture and opaque texture off unless a feature needs
  them; keep SRP Batcher on.
- Measure on the device, not the Editor: the Editor's GPU and driver differ from the phone's.

Texture and audio budgets apply through `TextureImporter` platform settings on owned assets only,
after previewing the paths. Keep color textures sRGB and data textures linear.

| Role | Starting budget | Inspect before accepting |
|---|---|---|
| World albedo | Max 1024 (2048 for hero assets); ASTC 6x6 | Compare on the device at gameplay distance |
| Normal maps | Max 1024; ASTC 5x5 or 4x4 | Shading artifacts on the low-end device |
| Packed masks | Max 512–1024; ASTC 6x6 | Required channels, metallic/smoothness artifacts |
| Screen-space UI | Match displayed size; ASTC 4x4 or RGBA32 for gradients | Edges at the device's density; keep slicing and atlas identity |

Mipmaps stay on for world textures. Audio: music and long ambience stream; short SFX decompress on
load; force mono for positional effects; keep sample rate content-driven; total installed size
stays inside the store's limits for the selected distribution.

### Thermals and battery

Sustained workloads can trigger thermal throttling depending on device, rendering cost, and ambient
conditions. Measure a soak run before choosing a 30 or 60 fps tier; consider the Adaptive Performance
package when measured behavior calls for runtime quality scaling. Its
automatic and manual performance modes work on Android providers; iOS controls CPU and GPU levels
itself. Test with a soak run (see step 5).

**Done:** the audit and numbered recommendations were shown and the user's explicit confirmation was received
before any change; every row has a status (Applied, Already correct, or Skipped with reason), and
re-reading the settings through the Editor API returns the target values.

## 4. Build profiles and CLI

Only the items confirmed in stage 4. Create Development and Release profiles only for the selected
platforms (Android and/or iOS) through the Editor or CLI. Unselected platforms need no profiles or hosts. Not every setting is isolated per profile in every Editor version, so inspect shared
Player Settings after saving.

| Choice | Development | Release |
|---|---|---|
| Development Build | On | Off |
| Script debugging / profiler | On only when needed; Deep Profiling off | Off |
| Output (Android) | `.apk`, `Builds/Android-Dev/` | `.aab`, `Builds/Android-Release/` |
| Output (iOS) | Xcode project, Debug configuration | Xcode project, archived in Release configuration |

Build from the CLI, one target per invocation (`-projectPath` and `-quit` are required;
`-batchmode` and `-logFile` are recommended):

```
Unity -batchmode -quit -projectPath <abs path> -activeBuildProfile <profile asset> -build <output path> -logFile <log>
```

Use `-buildTarget Android` or `iOS` when no profile asset exists, or `-executeMethod` for a custom
build script. Prefer the installed `unity` CLI when present and read its help for exact flags. An
iOS build only produces the Xcode project; archive and sign it with `xcodebuild` or Xcode on a Mac.

Preserve debug symbols for crash reporting (Android native symbols, iOS dSYMs).

**Done:** each selected release output builds on a suitable host (`.aab` on any supported host; the iOS Xcode
project archives on a Mac), or each missing host is marked Not verified.

## 5. Verify

Run the project's tests and read fresh results. On each selected platform, install the **release**
build on a physical low-end device and check:

- cold start time, then pause/resume, a phone call or notification interruption, and a screen lock
- orientation changes, safe-area layout on a notched device, and touch input at screen edges
- scene transitions, save/load, and quit and relaunch
- audio on first playback, with the silent switch (iOS) and with headphones plugged in and removed
- a 15–30 minute soak run on the Low tier showing stable frame time and no thermal throttling
- peak memory on the device (Memory Profiler) and install size against the store limit
- every permission prompt fires once, with the right description, only for permissions in use
- logs (`adb logcat` on Android, Xcode console on iOS) show no missing shaders, assets, or libraries

Android additionally: inspect the `.aab` for 16 KB alignment, and install through an internal test
track or `bundletool` rather than the Editor. iOS additionally: archive in Xcode, read the privacy
report, and validate the archive with App Store Connect (TestFlight).

**Done:** each check is Passed, Failed, or Not verified, with device model, OS version, graphics
API, and quality tier recorded beside every measurement.

## 6. Report

End with this table and a `git diff --stat ProjectSettings` summary:

| Item | Status | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| Each step 3 row | Applied / Already correct / Skipped | Old value → new value |
| Each unpicked recommendation | Proposal | Finding, proposed change, and risk |
| Each step 5 check | Passed / Failed / Not verified | Evidence, or the missing device, toolchain, or account |

Put unanswered target-contract items, store-requirement deadlines, unpicked recommendations that
need a decision, and failed checks in a separate block labelled "Needs your decision" at the top of
the report.

- [iOS Player settings](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/class-PlayerSettingsiOS.html)

> document". The agent audits your repository first and recommends licence-free GitHub checks, a pull
> request template, and optionally a workflow for your own test machine. You pick which to carry over;

# Set up CI for a Unity project (agent instructions)

Install continuous integration that works **without a paid Unity licence**. A Personal licence cannot be
activated on a hosted CI runner (the CLI's own generated workflow notes that `unity license activate
--personal` does not work there), so the default design runs everything that needs no Editor on a hosted
runner, and runs Editor tests locally or on a machine the user hosts. This document is self-contained.
It does not commit, push, register a runner, or store a secret. **Last verified: October 2026** (Git
2.54, .NET SDK 10.0, Unity CLI 1.0.0-beta.13, Unity 6000.7.0b4 and 6000.6.2f1).

Source (replace `main` with a commit SHA for a repeatable run):
`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/krogh-jacobsen/unity-code-style-guide/main/AuditInstructions/ContinuousIntegration/`

## What each tier does

| Tier | Runs where | Needs a Unity licence | Catches |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A. Project checks** (default) | GitHub-hosted runner | No | Missing/orphan metadata, duplicate GUIDs, static test-isolation candidates, ignored-test notices, Git settings, whitespace and naming violations |
| **B. Local test gate** (default) | The developer's machine | Their own | Failing EditMode and PlayMode tests, through `unity test` and a pull request checklist |
| **C. Self-hosted test runner** (opt-in) | A machine the user owns | Their own, already active | The same tests, run on every pull request |
| **D. Licensed hosted CI** (opt-in) | GitHub-hosted runner | Yes: a serial, floating, or offline licence | Tests and player builds. Use `unity ci init`, not these files |

Tier A never runs the Editor, so **a green run does not mean tests pass**. Say so wherever you report it.

## Operating rules

- Never write a licence, serial, token, or password into a workflow or file. Tier A uses no secrets.
- Do not enable Tier C on a public repository without the user's explicit approval of the risk below.
- Copy the shipped files unchanged except for the documented edit points. Do not commit or push.
- Report observed results separately from checks you could not run (**Not verified**).
- Without Unity CLI, continue the saved-file audit. For confirmed execution, run the Python/Git/.NET
  checks directly when those tools exist; mark only unavailable checks Not verified. Authorized
  Editor suites can use the Test Runner window instead of `unity test`. No CLI/bridge installation
  is implied by this workflow.

## Review, recommend, confirm

This document always runs in four stages. Nothing is written to the project until stage 4 ends in an
explicit user confirmation.

1. **Audit.** Read the project and report what already matches this document, what differs, and what
   could not be checked. Read-only.
2. **Recommend.** List every difference as a numbered recommendation: ID, finding, proposed change,
   why it matters, risk (low, medium, high), and a default (do or skip). List items that already
   match as "no change needed". Add recommendations of your own from what you found, including ones
   this document does not mention.
3. **Choose.** The user picks any subset of IDs, "all recommended", or none. Carry over only the
   picked items; unpicked items stay proposals in the report.
4. **Confirm.** Present the exact changes for the picked subset (files, settings, values, commands)
   and obtain explicit user authorization before making them, including saving the report.
   Confirmation need not contain the literal word "yes": after the concrete scope is presented,
   "implement R1 and R3" can both select and confirm those items. Selection alone ("R1 and R3")
   chooses scope without authorizing implementation. Honor existing authorization for unchanged
   scope without asking again; clarify a delayed reply only when its scope is materially ambiguous.
   Changed scope needs confirmation for the changed items. In a non-interactive session, or when
   authorization is absent, stop after stage 2 and change nothing.

Steps below that apply, install, or build run only after stage 4, and only for confirmed items. A new
finding during those steps becomes a new recommendation and returns to stage 3.

## 1. Preflight

This step is the audit input and changes nothing. Identify one Unity project and its repository. Record:

- The **host**. The workflows are GitHub Actions. For another host, install the scripts only and say the
  workflow is not provided (`unity ci init --provider gitlab` covers GitLab for licensed projects).
- **Project root versus repository root.** Tier A takes the project path from `UNITY_PROJECT_PATH`.
- Existing `.github/workflows/`, `.github/unity-ci/`, and `.github/pull_request_template.md`.
- An **`.editorconfig`** in the project or repository root. The style checks measure against it, so if it
  is missing, install the [EditorConfig starter](../../AgentsInstructions/CodeStyleGuide/EditorConfig/README.md) first or skip the style steps.
- Whether the repository is public or private, and `unity license status` on this machine.
- Whether tests exist (`Assets/**/Tests`, test asmdefs). Follow the [test setup guide](../Testing/TestingInstructions.md)
  when they do not.
- How each existing file compares with its shipped version. Fetch the shipped files into a temporary
  folder outside the project (not a project change) and mark each destination absent, identical, or
  different.

**Done:** host, roots, existing files and their comparison, `.editorconfig`, visibility, and test
presence are known, and the audit was shown to the user.

## 2. Ask and select

Ask in one batch, then show each tier as a numbered recommendation (stage 2) so the user can pick any
subset. The defaults below are recommended defaults: they still need the stage 4 confirmation. Apply
the default when the user says "use defaults".

| ID | Question | Recommended default |
|---|---|---|
| R1 | Tier A (licence-free GitHub checks)? | Do |
| R2 | Tier B (pull request template with a test checklist)? | Do |
| R3 | Tier C (self-hosted test workflow)? | Skip. Needs a runner you register, and the security note in the workflow |
| R4 | Style steps blocking from the first run, or report-only until the baseline is clean? | Report-only when the baseline run in step 4 has findings |

Add your own recommendations from the audit, such as a missing `.editorconfig` or a conflicting workflow.

**Done:** the audit and recommendation list were shown, the user's picks are recorded, and an explicit
yes to the exact file list was received before any change.

## 3. Install

Only the items confirmed in stage 4. Stage the files, check them, then copy. Files install to these destinations:

| Source | Destination | Tier |
|---|---|---|
| `Workflows/unity-checks.yml` | `.github/workflows/unity-checks.yml` | A |
| `Scripts/check_unity_project.py` | `.github/unity-ci/check_unity_project.py` | A |
| `Scripts/Lint.csproj` | `.github/unity-ci/Lint.csproj` | A |
| `Workflows/pull_request_template.md` | `.github/pull_request_template.md` | B |
| `Workflows/unity-tests-self-hosted.yml` | `.github/workflows/unity-tests-self-hosted.yml` | C |

1. **Stage** into a temporary folder and reject HTML or error responses.
2. **Destinations.** Absent: install. Identical: leave it. Different content: a conflict. Show both and
   resolve it before copying; never overwrite a project's own workflow or template.
3. **Edit points**, and only these: `UNITY_PROJECT_PATH` in both selected workflow files when the
   project is a repository subfolder (and the matching `Lint.csproj` exclusions if the project has more vendor or
   sample folders); the `branches:` list when the default branch is not `main`.
4. If the style gate is report-only, add `continue-on-error: true` to the two `dotnet format` steps and
   say that is temporary.

**Done:** every confirmed file is installed or identical, and the edit points are the only differences.

## 4. Run the checks locally first

Applies to the installed tiers only. A new gate often fails on the existing code. Learn the baseline before the first push. Run from the repository
root (where `.github/` lives), exporting the absolute Unity project path, including any subfolder:

```bash
export UNITY_PROJECT_PATH="/absolute/repository/path/to/UnityProject"
python3 .github/unity-ci/check_unity_project.py --project "$UNITY_PROJECT_PATH"
unity vcs doctor "$UNITY_PROJECT_PATH"
dotnet restore .github/unity-ci/Lint.csproj
dotnet format whitespace .github/unity-ci/Lint.csproj --no-restore --verify-no-changes
dotnet format style .github/unity-ci/Lint.csproj --no-restore --diagnostics IDE1006 --severity info --verify-no-changes
```

Read each exit code. `unity vcs doctor` exits 4 on a finding. `dotnet format` exits 2 when it would
change something. Report the count per check. Offer to fix formatting with
`dotnet format whitespace <Lint.csproj>`, but only on the user's own code and only with approval: it
rewrites files. Without the .NET SDK or the Unity CLI locally, report those checks as **Not verified**.

**Done:** each check has a baseline result, and the style-gate mode is chosen from it.

## 5. The local test gate (Tier B, only when confirmed)

The pull request template tells reviewers what was run. The commands are in the
[test setup guide](../Testing/TestingInstructions.md):

```bash
unity test /absolute/project --mode EditMode --output /absolute/results/editmode.xml
unity test /absolute/project --mode PlayMode --output /absolute/results/playmode.xml
```

Close the project in the Editor first. Exit code 8 means tests failed; 6 means the run itself failed.
Read the result XML, not just the exit code. Run them now if the user agrees, and report passed,
failed, skipped, and `[Ignore]`d counts from the files.

**Done:** the user has the commands, and the suites were run or the gap is stated.

## 6. The self-hosted workflow (Tier C, only when confirmed)

Registering a runner is the user's action: it needs a token from their repository settings. Give these steps and do
not perform them.

1. Settings > Actions > Runners > New self-hosted runner, on the machine that has the Editor, and add the
   label `unity`.
2. The runner service must run as the user whose Editor licence is active. `unity license status` must show it.
3. Set the workflow's `UNITY_PROJECT_PATH` to the intended project under `${{ github.workspace }}`.
   Its `ProjectVersion.txt` selects the required installed Editor; the project must not be open in it.
   Preflight runs in that directory, and both test commands name it explicitly.
4. **Security.** A self-hosted runner executes the code of whatever it checks out. The workflow is limited
   to branches in the same repository and manual dispatch. Keep the repository private, or understand
   that a contributor with write access can run code on that machine.
5. Run the workflow once with **Run workflow** (`workflow_dispatch`) and read the uploaded results.

**Done:** the steps were given, and the first run is observed by the user or reported as **Not verified**.

## 7. Verify

- The Tier A files match the source, and `.github/unity-ci/` holds both scripts.
- Step 4's commands ran (or are reported **Not verified**).
- The workflow files are valid YAML and contain no secret or licence reference.
- A real GitHub run needs a push, which only the user approves. After one, read the run summary: it
  lists errors and states that Editor tests did not run. Until then report the hosted run as **Not verified**.

**Done:** each installed tier has a verification result or a specific Not verified reason.

## 8. Report

| Item | Status | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| Source URL and revision | | |
| Recommendations picked and confirmed | R-IDs applied | The exact change list the user confirmed |
| Recommendations not picked | Proposal | R-IDs left open, with the default and risk |
| Tier A files | Installed / Identical / Conflict | Paths |
| Tier B template | Installed / Identical / Declined | |
| Tier C workflow | Installed / Declined | Runner registered by the user? |
| Baseline per check | Pass / N findings / Not verified | meta and tests, doctor, whitespace, naming |
| Style gate mode | Blocking / Report-only | |
| Editor tests | Run locally / Not run | Counts from the result files |
| Hosted run | Observed / Not verified | |

Put conflicts, a failing baseline, the unpicked recommendations, and the Tier C security choice in a
"Needs your decision" block at the top. Say plainly that Tier A does not run tests.

**Done:** every selected tier and unpicked recommendation is accounted for, including hosted-run limits.

## For users with a licence

Use `unity ci init` (`--provider github` or `gitlab`, `--shards N` to split tests) instead of these
workflows. It generates a complete pipeline: it installs the Editor, restores caches, activates a
licence, runs tests, and builds. Its licence step takes a serial, a floating server, or an offline
licence file as a secret, and it states that `--personal` activation does not work in CI. Tier A files
still complement it as the fast first job.

> How it works: give this URL to your agent, for example "Prepare my Unity project for the CoreCLR
> migration using this document". The agent audits your project, asks which Editor and platforms you
> are targeting, and recommends fixes. You pick which to carry over; nothing changes before you
> confirm, and it works on an isolated branch and reports what it verified. Human overview:
> [readme](README.md).

# CoreCLR migration (agent instructions)

**This guide is work in progress.** It prepares a project for Unity's move from Mono to CoreCLR. This
document is self-contained and experimental: load it for an actual runtime migration, not for normal
starter setup. The selected starter stays on the engine and language profile in
[UnityTechStack.md](../../AgentsInstructions/UnityTechStack/UnityTechStack.md).
**Last verified: October 2026** (sources read 2026-10-12). The roadmap moves often, so re-read the
two linked Unity posts before relying on any date or version below.

## Current evidence versus roadmap

Unity's [October 2026 update](https://discussions.unity.com/t/coreclr-scripting-and-net-update-october-2026/1738338)
announces a Unity 7.0 Alpha CoreCLR Editor initially targeting C# 9 and .NET Standard 2.1. Full .NET 10
and C# 14 remain a staged target with no committed public date. Unity 6.7 experimental players are
separate compatibility options. Do not turn an earlier 6.8 forecast into a baseline guarantee.

The [official upgrade guide](https://discussions.unity.com/t/path-to-coreclr-2026-upgrade-guide/1714279)
is a living source. Compare it with the exact chosen Editor's assemblies and documentation before
writing migration code. Availability of an API in a roadmap does not establish player or platform support.

## Operating rules

- Audit saved project evidence read-only, including on a dirty tree, with existing work preserved.
  Perform confirmed migration execution in an isolated copy or checkout; a branch alone does not
  isolate files from an active Editor. Resolve isolation before execution, without blocking independent audit.
- Use `unity-cli` for compilation, repeated Play, tests, and builds. Resolve packages through
  CLI-invoked Package Manager Client operations. Leave ProjectSettings YAML and `.meta` files untouched.
- Preserve unsaved scenes and the user's other edits. Keep experimental results separate from the
  starter's tested baseline.
- Confirm each API, namespace, and attribute against the **installed** Editor's assemblies before
  using it. Prefer evidence of a supported API over a guessed define; do not invent
  `UNITY_6_8_OR_NEWER`, because engine defines follow actual version numbering.
- Do not promise performance gains. Record a check as **Not verified** when its Editor, platform
  module, or device is missing.

## Review, recommend, confirm

This document always runs in four stages. Nothing is written to the project until stage 4 ends in an
explicit user confirmation.

1. **Audit.** Read the project and report what already matches this document, what differs, and what
   could not be checked. Read-only.
2. **Recommend.** List every difference as a numbered recommendation: ID, finding, proposed change,
   why it matters, risk (low, medium, high), and a default (do or skip). List items that already
   match as "no change needed". Add recommendations of your own from what you found, including ones
   this document does not mention.
3. **Choose.** The user picks any subset of IDs, "all recommended", or none. Carry over only the
   picked items; unpicked items stay proposals in the report.
4. **Confirm.** Present the exact changes for the picked subset (files, settings, values, commands)
   and obtain explicit user authorization before making them, including saving the report.
   Confirmation need not contain the literal word "yes": after the concrete scope is presented,
   "implement R1 and R3" can both select and confirm those items. Selection alone ("R1 and R3")
   chooses scope without authorizing implementation. Honor existing authorization for unchanged
   scope without asking again; clarify a delayed reply only when its scope is materially ambiguous.
   Changed scope needs confirmation for the changed items. In a non-interactive session, or when
   authorization is absent, stop after stage 2 and change nothing.

Steps below that apply, install, or build run only after stage 4, and only for confirmed items. A new
finding during those steps becomes a new recommendation and returns to stage 3.

## 1. Preflight

This step is the audit input and changes nothing. Read the project, then summarise it in one table
(item, current value):

- Editor version (`ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt`) and the migration Editor to install or use.
- Scripting backend and API Compatibility Level per platform; installed platform modules.
- Every package in `Packages/manifest.json` and `Packages/packages-lock.json`, plus native plugins and
  precompiled assemblies (`.dll`) under `Assets`.
- Assembly definitions, so each finding in step 3 maps to an owning assembly.
- Baseline evidence already available: compile result, EditMode and PlayMode test results, and one
  normal player build on the current Editor, with their revision/freshness. Do not launch these during
  read-only preflight. Missing results are Not verified; propose fresh baseline runs in the confirmation
  list. Without comparable results, later failures cannot be attributed.

**Done:** the table exists, every row has a known value, observed absence, or Not verified reason; baseline results are recorded
or marked Not verified with the reason, and the audit was shown to the user.

## 2. Ask the migration contract

Ask all questions in one batch; the project cannot answer them. Apply the default when the user says
"use defaults"; defaults are recommended defaults that still need the stage 4 confirmation.

| Question | Default |
|---|---|
| Which exact migration Editor (Unity 7.0 Alpha CoreCLR Editor, or a 6.7 experimental player)? | No default; ask, and record the version |
| Which platforms and scripting backends must be tested? | The Editor plus one normal player build on the host platform |
| Isolated checkout or copy ready? | Propose a separate checkout or copy; defer migration execution if declined, while completing independent read-only audit |
| Which dependencies are third-party, and who owns each? | Every non-Unity entry in `packages-lock.json` and every `.dll` |
| Which saved-data fixtures exist (old saves, serialized ScriptableObjects)? | None: persistence checks become Not verified |

**Done:** every question has an answer or a stated default, repeated back to the user, one line each.

## 3. Inventory and apply

Scan owned code first, then dependencies. The scan is the audit: report every finding with its file
and owning assembly, and give each fixable finding a recommendation ID (stage 2) with a default of
skip, so the default outcome is a report and no fix. Apply a fix only for findings the user picked and
confirmed in stage 4, one assembly at a time.

| Area | Find | Resolve | Condition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mutable statics and events | `static` fields that are not `readonly` or `const`; `static event` declarations; static collections | Reset at a lifecycle boundary chosen after inspecting the installed lifecycle APIs (below); prove the reset across Play and code reload | Fix when picked and confirmed |
| Retained assembly references | `Assembly.Load`, cached `Type` or reflection results, `AppDomain` use | Release at teardown; use `BeforeCodeUnloading` only if the installed Editor exposes it | Fix when picked and confirmed |
| Source-asset runtime writes | ScriptableObject or prefab fields written during Play | Copy to runtime state, or reset on teardown, so the source asset stays clean | Fix when picked and confirmed |
| Owned threads and native resources | `Thread`, `Task.Run`, native handles, `NativeArray`, `ComputeBuffer`, other `IDisposable` owners | Dispose at the owner's lifetime end; observe async errors | Fix when picked and confirmed |
| Dependency framework targets | Each package and `.dll` target framework; native plugins; platform and AOT restrictions | Update, replace, or record as incompatible; never silently drop a dependency | Report always |
| Persisted data | Serializers an unsupported API depends on (`BinaryFormatter` is the usual case) | A format and ownership migration with a versioned save fixture; a JSON rename alone is not a safe old-save migration | Fix when picked and confirmed |
| New lifecycle attributes | Any attribute from the next paragraph | Compile with its required namespace and the exact supported Editor/version gate | When used |

**Lifecycle APIs.** The official guide demonstrates `Unity.Scripting.LifecycleManagement.AfterCodeReloadSerialization`
and discusses `AutoStaticsCleanup` and `BeforeCodeUnloading`. These are not blanket instructions to
annotate every static class: read the installed API, choose per field, and compile. The repository's
[static-state policy](../ProjectSettings/ProjectSettings.md) is an optional pointer for the reload decision.

**Done:** the audit and recommendation list were shown and explicit user confirmation was received before any
change, every finding is listed with its assembly and a disposition (fixed, proposal, or
incompatible), and every attribute used compiles on the target Editor.

## 4. Verify

Run through `unity-cli` against the migration Editor, reading fresh XML and logs:

- Compile with zero errors and no new warnings for owned assemblies.
- EditMode and PlayMode tests; compare counts and ignored tests with the step 1 baseline.
- Enter and exit Play at least twice, then trigger a code reload: owned state resets and a static
  counter or subscriber from the previous run is gone.
- Load every saved-data fixture from step 2 and read back the values.
- Exercise async and resource teardown, and the project's Editor tools.
- Build each agreed player target and run it.

**Manual fallback:** the selected Editor, Package Manager, Test Runner, and build settings.

**Done:** each check above has a result or a Not verified reason, backed by a fresh log or XML file.

## 5. Report

Report in this shape:

```
<One sentence: what now works on which Editor.>

| Component | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| <assembly, package, or system> | Works / Incompatible / Not verified | <command → result> |

Applied (confirmed): <recommendation IDs, with the change list the user confirmed>
Proposals (not picked): <recommendation IDs, with default and risk>
Measured: <numbers, or "none taken">
Not verified: <check → why>
```

Record incompatible and unverified components explicitly, with measured results. Do not claim a
performance gain unless it was measured on the migration Editor.

**Done:** the report covers every component from step 1, lists confirmed items as applied and
unpicked recommendations as proposals, and no row is blank.

## Rollback

If the migration Editor cannot open the project, or the baseline cannot be restored, stop and revert
the branch. Report the Editor version, the first failing step, and the log lines; leave the user's
original working tree untouched.

## Needs your decision

Put these in a "Needs your decision" block in the report, one bullet each, with the recommendation inline:

- **Which unpicked recommendations to carry over later.** Recommended: keep them as proposals until
  the migration Editor is chosen and the baseline is known.
- **Which migration Editor to target.** Recommended: the Unity 7.0 Alpha CoreCLR Editor for an
  Editor-side trial; a 6.7 experimental player only to probe player compatibility.
- **Whether to accept an incompatible dependency.** Recommended: no; replace it or defer the migration.
- **Whether to merge fixes made for the migration.** Recommended: merge only changes that also pass
  on the current Editor.

> How it works: give this URL to your agent, for example "Review my current folder structure
> against this guide and recommend what and how to improve", or add "and move things in small,
> verified batches" to reorganize. The agent audits first and recommends, you pick what to carry
> over, and nothing moves before you confirm the exact change list. Human overview: [readme](README.md).

# Review and reorganize an existing project's folders (agent instructions)

Compare a project that already has content and its own folder structure against the layout below,
recommend improvements, and, only when the user opts in, move content in small reversible batches.
This document is self-contained. For a brand-new project, use [SetupFolders.md](SetupFolders.md)
instead. **Last verified: October 2026.**

## Operating rules

- Start in **review** mode: read and report only. Move nothing until the user has picked items and
  confirmed the exact batch list (stages 3 and 4 below).
- Move imported assets only through Editor APIs (`AssetDatabase.ValidateMoveAsset`, then
  `AssetDatabase.MoveAsset`) or the Project window. Unity ties references to the GUID in each
  `.meta` file, and moving files outside the Editor risks disconnecting the GUID from the file.
  Treat a non-empty string returned by `MoveAsset` as a failure and stop.
- Checkpoints apply to confirmed move batches, not to read-only audit. Continue independent audit
  with user edits and unsaved scenes preserved. Before a move batch, agree a reversible checkpoint
  and resolve edits that overlap its paths; do not stash, commit, or save unrelated work.
- Leave `Packages/`, `ProjectSettings/`, and vendor content with a required layout where they are.
- Keep a move log (old path, new path, GUID) in the conversation; it is the rollback record.
- Stop at the first error, compile failure, or unexpected change. Report it; never push through.
- Mark checks you cannot run **Not verified**.

## Review, recommend, confirm

This document always runs in four stages. Nothing is written to the project until stage 4 ends in an
explicit user confirmation.

1. **Audit.** Read the project and report what already matches this document, what differs, and what
   could not be checked. Read-only.
2. **Recommend.** List every difference as a numbered recommendation: ID, finding, proposed change,
   why it matters, risk (low, medium, high), and a default (do or skip). List items that already
   match as "no change needed". Add recommendations of your own from what you found, including ones
   this document does not mention.
3. **Choose.** The user picks any subset of IDs, "all recommended", or none. Carry over only the
   picked items; unpicked items stay proposals in the report.
4. **Confirm.** Present the exact changes for the picked subset (files, settings, values, commands)
   and obtain explicit user authorization before making them, including saving the report.
   Confirmation need not contain the literal word "yes": after the concrete scope is presented,
   "implement R1 and R3" can both select and confirm those items. Selection alone ("R1 and R3")
   chooses scope without authorizing implementation. Honor existing authorization for unchanged
   scope without asking again; clarify a delayed reply only when its scope is materially ambiguous.
   Changed scope needs confirmation for the changed items. In a non-interactive session, or when
   authorization is absent, stop after stage 2 and change nothing.

Steps below that apply, install, or build run only after stage 4, and only for confirmed items. A new
finding during those steps becomes a new recommendation and returns to stage 3.

## 1. Preflight

Read the project's own instructions first; they win over this document. Then record:

- Editor version and whether the Editor is open. Moves need the Editor (or an Editor-driven CLI
  command); a review alone can read the files directly.
- Source-control state, and whether the project compiles cleanly now. Do not start moves on a
  project with compile errors.
- Existing test/compile evidence: record revision, freshness, and known failures. Missing evidence
  is Not verified; new test or compilation runs belong in the confirmed execution plan.
- The `Assets` tree to three levels, with file counts and the longest asset path.
- Template leftovers (`Assets/Settings`, sample scene and assets), vendor folders (Asset Store or
  package-style content with its own layout), and any `Resources`, `StreamingAssets`, `Plugins`,
  `Editor`, or `Gizmos` folders and where they sit.
- Assembly definitions and references, and each script's effective assembly.

**Done:** the inventory and baseline exist, you can state which parts you will treat as vendor, and
nothing has been changed.

## 2. Ask

Ask in one batch. The defaults are recommended answers that still need stages 3 and 4, even when the
user says "use defaults".

| Question | Default |
|---|---|
| Review only, or also reorganize? | Review only |
| Whole project or specific folders or features? | Whole `Assets`, owned content only |
| Adopt the whole layout or only parts? | Parts: keep the project's convention where it is consistent, and fix inconsistencies |
| Move scripts and asmdefs? | No: propose them, move only after separate approval |
| Move path-dependent content (`Resources`, Addressables, `StreamingAssets`)? | No |
| Checkpoint method (commit or stash)? | Commit |

**Done:** the mode and scope are agreed and repeated back in one line each.

## 3. Review against the layout

The target layout, as a menu rather than a mandate:

```text
ArtSource/                # Optional, beside Assets: PSD, Blend, other source files
Packages/                 # Reusable code as embedded packages
Assets/
├── ScriptTemplates/  StreamingAssets/  ThirdPartyAssets/   # direct children when used
├── Settings/Presets/     # Import presets (the starter's convention)
└── {ProjectName}/
    ├── Scenes/  Settings/  Shared/  SceneTemplates/
    └── {Feature}/        # Scenes, Scripts, Editor, Tests, Data, Prefabs, Art, UI
```

Check each area, citing a path as evidence for every finding:

| Area | Look for |
|---|---|
| Organization | Type-first folders (`Scripts`, `Prefabs` at the root) instead of feature-first; duplicate or ambiguous roots (`Scripts` and `Code`); loose assets in the `Assets` root |
| Naming | Spaces, mixed casing, case-only duplicates, dot-prefixed names (Unity skips them on import), accidental `~` suffixes |
| Depth and paths | Nesting beyond about four levels below the content root; very long asset paths |
| Ownership | Content under a feature that other features own, and `Shared` content that depends on feature code or assets; dependency cycles between features |
| Special folders | `StreamingAssets` or `ScriptTemplates` not direct children of `Assets`; `Resources` used for convenience instead of a loading need; `Plugins`, `Editor`, or `Gizmos` placed where they change compilation or behavior |
| Assemblies | Scripts outside any intended asmdef; `Editor` folders inside runtime asmdefs without Editor-only assemblies; test asmdefs that cannot reference production assemblies |
| Vendor content | Vendor files mixed with owned content; vendor files modified in place |
| Source art | PSD, Blend, or other source files inside `Assets` |
| Template leftovers | Unused sample scenes and assets |

Rate each finding **Risk** (likely to cause bugs or build failures), **Improve** (clear benefit), or
**Optional** (taste), and give its **move risk** from the next table.

### Move risk

Moves are safe when only GUIDs refer to the asset, and dangerous where a path, folder name, or
folder position carries meaning.

| Move risk | Content | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Low | Prefabs, materials, textures, models, audio, ScriptableObject assets, UI files, and scenes, moved between ordinary folders | Unity references them by GUID, and the Editor moves the `.meta` file with the asset |
| Medium | Scripts, asmdefs, asmrefs, and anything moved into or out of an `Editor`, `Plugins`, or `Standard Assets` folder | Folder position selects the compile phase and assembly, and an asmdef covers the whole folder tree beneath it, so a move can change which assembly a script belongs to |
| High | `Resources` contents, Addressables, `StreamingAssets` contents, hard-coded `"Assets/..."` strings, import presets and postprocessors scoped by path, CI and `.gitignore` or LFS patterns | Their meaning depends on the path text. Unity's Addressables default address is the asset path, so a moved asset's address can change |
| Leave | `Packages/`, `ProjectSettings/`, vendor content with a required layout, template-created `Assets/Settings`, `Editor Default Resources`, and the special folders themselves | Unity or the vendor expects them where they are |

Before rating anything Medium or High, search the project for `Resources.Load`, hard-coded `Assets/`
paths, Addressables addresses, and path-scoped presets, and record what you find.

**Done:** every finding has evidence, a severity, and a move risk, and every High item has the
code or configuration that depends on it listed. The findings are the audit stage's output.

## 4. Recommend and plan

Present the review: a short summary, the findings table, and what to leave alone, with each finding
as a numbered recommendation (ID, evidence, proposed change, risk, default). Then offer a plan
only if the user asked to reorganize, as ordered batches:

1. Create missing target folders (follow the naming rules: PascalCase, no spaces, no leading dot).
2. Rename and case fixes. On a case-insensitive file system, move a case-only rename through a
   temporary name, and check the result in the Editor.
3. Low-risk content, one feature at a time.
4. Scripts and asmdefs, one assembly at a time (only if approved).
5. High-risk items, only on explicit request and with a stated verification for each.

Each batch lists its moves (old path → new path), the expected effect, the risk, the checks that
prove it, and how to undo it. Keep batches small enough to review: one feature or one assembly.

**Done:** the user has picked specific recommendations and confirmed the exact batches in stage 4,
or chosen review only. The per-batch checkpoints in step 5 stay as extra safety on top of that gate.

## 5. Apply one batch at a time

Only the items confirmed in stage 4 are moved. For each confirmed batch:

1. Checkpoint, then run `ValidateMoveAsset` for every move; resolve any non-empty result first.
2. Move through `MoveAsset`, requiring an empty return each time. Run `AssetDatabase.SaveAssets` and
   `Refresh`, and wait for compilation to finish.
3. Verify (step 6). On success, commit the batch with the move log in the message.
4. On any failure, undo the batch by moving the assets back through `MoveAsset` using the move log.
   If the Editor state is unreliable, close it and restore the checkpoint with source control.

**Done:** the audit and recommendation list were shown and confirmed before batch 1, and the batch is
committed with verification passed, or fully undone with the cause reported.

## 6. Verify each batch

- Every moved asset keeps its GUID (`AssetDatabase.AssetPathToGUID` before and after).
- The project compiles with no new errors, and each moved script's effective assembly is unchanged
  (compare before and after, for example with `CompilationPipeline.GetAssemblyNameFromScriptPath`).
- Open the scenes and prefabs of the affected features: no missing references or scripts.
- The build scene list still points at existing scenes. Check it; do not assume it updated.
- The project's tests pass, matching the baseline, and Play Mode starts the affected scenes.
- Path-dependent items found in step 3 still resolve: `Resources.Load` names, string paths,
  Addressables addresses, preset and postprocessor filters, CI and ignore patterns.
- After script or assembly batches, a build for a representative player target compiles.

**Done:** each check is Passed, Failed, or Not verified, and any failure has been undone or fixed.

## 7. Report

| Item | Status | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| Each finding | Risk / Improve / Optional | Path, evidence, recommendation, move risk |
| Unpicked recommendations | Proposal | ID and reason left open |
| Each batch | Applied / Undone / Not started | Moves, commit, checks |
| Each check | Passed / Failed / Not verified | Evidence |
| Left alone | Vendor / Leave | Path and reason |

Put open questions, unpicked recommendations that need a ruling, and failed checks in a
"Needs your decision" block at the top.

## References

- [Special folders and script compilation order](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/SpecialFolders.html)
- [AssetDatabase.MoveAsset](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/AssetDatabase.MoveAsset.html)
- [Assembly definition references](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/assembly-definitions-referencing.html)
- [Custom package layout](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/cus-layout.html)
- [Organizing your Unity project](https://unity.com/how-to/organizing-your-project)

> How it works: give this URL to your agent, for example "Set up folders only in my Unity project
> from this document". The agent audits the project, recommends the folders that fit, lets you pick
> which to carry over, and creates nothing until you confirm the exact list. Then it reports what it
