> How it works: give this URL to your agent, for example "Set up Git for my Unity project from this
> document". The agent audits the project's Git rules, recommends what to install, lets you pick which
> to carry over, and writes nothing until you confirm the exact change list. Then it verifies the
> result with Git. It changes nothing in the Unity project. Human overview: [readme](README.md).

# Set up version control for a Unity project (agent instructions)

Install a Unity `.gitignore` and `.gitattributes` into an existing project, then verify them. This
document is self-contained. It does not commit, push, rewrite history, or untrack files without the
user's approval, and it changes no Unity setting. **Last verified: October 2026** (Git 2.54, Git LFS
3.8.0, Unity CLI 1.0.0-beta.13, Unity 6000.7.0b4 and 6000.6.2f1).

Source (replace `main` with a commit SHA for a repeatable run):
`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/krogh-jacobsen/unity-code-style-guide/main/AuditInstructions/VersionControl/`
Two files: `Unity.gitignore` and `Unity.gitattributes`.

## Operating rules

- **Managed blocks only.** Each file is one block between `# BEGIN unity-code-style-guide: …` and
  `# END unity-code-style-guide: …` lines. Insert it, or replace the previous copy in place, and
  leave every line outside it exactly as it is. A project's own rules stay.
- Never commit, push, `git rm`, `git filter-repo`, or change `.git/config` or hooks without approval.
  Show the command and its effect first.
- Never hand-edit Unity files. Serialization and meta-file settings are read, not changed, here.
- Report observed results separately from checks you could not run (**Not verified**).

## Review, recommend, confirm

This document always runs in four stages. Nothing is written to the project until stage 4 ends in an
explicit user confirmation.

1. **Audit.** Read the project and report what already matches this document, what differs, and what
   could not be checked. Read-only.
2. **Recommend.** List every difference as a numbered recommendation: ID, finding, proposed change,
   why it matters, risk (low, medium, high), and a default (do or skip). List items that already
   match as "no change needed". Add recommendations of your own from what you found, including ones
   this document does not mention.
3. **Choose.** The user picks any subset of IDs, "all recommended", or none. Carry over only the
   picked items; unpicked items stay proposals in the report.
4. **Confirm.** Present the exact changes for the picked subset (files, settings, values, commands)
   and obtain explicit user authorization before making them, including saving the report.
   Confirmation need not contain the literal word "yes": after the concrete scope is presented,
   "implement R1 and R3" can both select and confirm those items. Selection alone ("R1 and R3")
   chooses scope without authorizing implementation. Honor existing authorization for unchanged
   scope without asking again; clarify a delayed reply only when its scope is materially ambiguous.
   Changed scope needs confirmation for the changed items. In a non-interactive session, or when
   authorization is absent, stop after stage 2 and change nothing.

Steps below that apply, install, or build run only after stage 4, and only for confirmed items. A new
finding during those steps becomes a new recommendation and returns to stage 3.

## 1. Preflight

Identify one Unity project (it contains `Assets` and `ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt`) and its Git
repository. Record:

- **Project root versus repository root.** The ignore rules start with `/`, so `.gitignore` goes in the
  **project root**. `.gitattributes` goes in the **repository root**. They are the same folder in most
  projects. If the project sits in a subfolder of a larger repository, say so.
- Whether the folder is a Git repository, and its remote. Do not run `git init` or create a remote
  unless asked; `unity vcs setup` exists for creating one.
- Existing `.gitignore` and `.gitattributes`, and whether either already holds a managed block here.
- `git --version`, `git lfs version` (installed? hooks present in this repository?), and whether the
  `unity` CLI is available (`unity vcs doctor --help`).
- **Settings that decide whether any of this works:** *Asset Serialization* is Force Text and
  *Version Control Mode* is Visible Meta Files (Project Settings > Editor and Version Control; the
  [project settings guide](../ProjectSettings/ProjectSettings.md) owns them). With the CLI,
  `unity vcs doctor` reports both. Without it, read `ProjectSettings/EditorSettings.asset`
  (`m_SerializationMode: 2`) and `ProjectSettings/VersionControlSettings.asset` (`m_Mode: Visible Meta Files`).
- Tracked files these rules would now exclude, after step 3.

**Done:** project root, repository root, existing rules, tool availability, and the two settings are
known, and no file has been written.

## 2. Ask and select

Ask in one batch. The defaults are recommended answers: they become recommendations that still go
through stages 3 and 4, even when the user says "use defaults".

| Question | Default |
|---|---|
| Keep `Assets/ThirdPartyAssets/` out of Git? Contributors then re-import vendor assets, and CI needs a way to fetch them | Yes, the starter's [folder layout](../FolderStructure/SetupFolders.md) convention. **Warn about clean clones and CI before applying** |
| Use Git LFS for textures, models, audio, video and source art? | Yes when `git lfs` is installed, otherwise no (report it) |
| Configure scene and prefab merging (`unity vcs merge-setup`)? | Yes when the `unity` CLI and the project's Editor are present |
| Install LFS hooks in this repository (`git lfs install --local`)? | Yes when LFS is selected |
| Commit the result? | No: leave the files in the working tree |

**Done:** the three choices (ThirdPartyAssets, LFS, merge setup) are explicit recommendations the
user has picked or declined.

## 3. Install

Only the items confirmed in stage 4 are installed.

1. **Stage.** Download both files into a temporary folder outside the project. Reject HTML or error
   responses. Each file must contain exactly one `BEGIN unity-code-style-guide` and one `END` line.
2. **Trim by choice.** If the user declined a section, delete it with its marker lines from the
   staged copy: `# BEGIN ThirdPartyAssets` to `# END ThirdPartyAssets` in the ignore file, and
   `# BEGIN LFS` to `# END LFS` in the attributes file. Nothing else is removed.
3. **Apply.**

   | Destination state | Action |
   |---|---|
   | File absent | Write the staged block as the file |
   | File exists, no block | Append the block after a blank line |
   | Block present and identical | Already installed: leave it |
   | Block present and different | Replace only the lines from `BEGIN` to `END` |

   If a project rule outside the block contradicts the block (for example `!*.log` or a rule that
   ignores `.meta` files), keep it and report it: a project may override, but an ignored `.meta` file
   breaks references.
4. **Merge setup (if selected).** `unity vcs merge-setup` writes a managed block of
   `merge=unityyamlmerge` attributes to `.gitattributes` and the merge driver to the repository's
   `.git/config`, then proves it with a test merge. The driver names an absolute Editor path, so it is
   **per clone** and each contributor runs it once. Run `--check` first. Without the CLI, report merge
   setup as **Not verified** and point to the manual route in the
   [Unity manual](https://docs.unity.com/en-us/engine/6000.7/manual/get-started/project-configuration/version-control/smart-merge)
   (the tool is `Contents/Helpers/UnityYAMLMerge` in a macOS Editor and
   `Editor\Data\Tools\UnityYAMLMerge.exe` on Windows).
5. **LFS hooks (if selected).** Run `git lfs install --local` once approved.

**Done:** the audit and recommendation list were shown and confirmed before any write, both files
hold the current block for the confirmed items, the declined sections are absent, and a repeat run
changes nothing.

## 4. Files Git already tracks

Run `git ls-files -ci --exclude-standard`. It lists tracked files that the new rules exclude. Group the
output (generated folders, vendor content, captures, other) and propose, per group, the safe fix:
`git rm -r --cached <path>`. That removes the files from Git and keeps them on disk, but **on the next
pull every teammate's working copy of those files is deleted**. Spell that out for vendor content
(`Assets/ThirdPartyAssets`) before asking. Apply nothing without approval.

Large binaries already in history remain there after an ignore or LFS change. If the repository has
them, report it and point to `unity vcs git migrate-lfs`, which prints a history-rewriting command.
Do not run it: rewriting shared history needs the whole team's agreement.

**Done:** every tracked-but-excluded group is reported with its proposed action, or none exist.

## 5. Verify

1. **Ignore behavior.** `git check-ignore -v` on these sample paths must match: `Library/x`,
   `Logs/x`, `ProfilerCaptures/capture.data`, `MemoryCaptures/a.snap`, `Builds/Win/Game.exe`,
   and, when selected, `Assets/ThirdPartyAssets/Vendor/x.cs`. These must not match:
   `Assets/<Root>/Scripts/x.cs`, its `.cs.meta`, `ProjectSettings/ProjectSettings.asset`,
   `Packages/manifest.json`, and `Packages/packages-lock.json`.
2. **Attributes.** `git check-attr filter eol -- <path>` shows `filter: lfs` for a PNG, FBX and WAV
   (when LFS is selected), and `eol: lf` for a `.cs` and `.unity` file.
3. **Unity's checker.** `unity vcs doctor` should report nothing. With ThirdPartyAssets excluded it also
   reports `META_FILES_IGNORED` while that folder's `.meta` exists locally; that finding is expected (a
   clean clone does not trigger it), and any other finding is real. Without the CLI, report this as **Not verified**.
4. **Working tree.** `git status --short` lists the new or changed files and no Unity-generated folder.
5. **Settings.** Force Text and Visible Meta Files are confirmed in the preflight, or reported as gaps.

**Done:** each check is observed, or its absence is stated.

## 6. Report

| Item | Status | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| Source URL and revision | | |
| Audit and recommendations shown, confirmation received | Yes / Stopped before confirming | Items picked |
| Unpicked recommendations | Proposal | ID and reason |
| `.gitignore` | Installed / Updated / Already installed | Path |
| `.gitattributes` | Installed / Updated / Already installed | Path |
| ThirdPartyAssets excluded | Yes / No | Folder present? |
| LFS section and hooks | Applied / Declined / Not available | Git LFS version |
| Merge setup | Configured / Declined / Not verified | Editor used |
| Tracked-but-excluded files | None / N groups | Proposed commands |
| Ignore and attribute behavior | Passed / Not verified | |
| `unity vcs doctor` | Clean / Findings / Not verified | |
| Force Text and Visible Meta Files | Confirmed / Gap | |

Put the tracked-but-excluded groups, the ThirdPartyAssets warning, any contradicting project rule, and
unpicked recommendations that need a ruling in a "Needs your decision" block at the top. Close with what each contributor does once after cloning:
`git lfs install`, `unity vcs merge-setup`, and re-importing the excluded vendor assets. Continuous
integration needs Git LFS on its checkout step and a source for the excluded assets.

> document". The agent audits your repository first and recommends licence-free GitHub checks, a pull
> request template, and optionally a workflow for your own test machine. You pick which to carry over;

# Set up CI for a Unity project (agent instructions)

Install continuous integration that works **without a paid Unity licence**. A Personal licence cannot be
activated on a hosted CI runner (the CLI's own generated workflow notes that `unity license activate
--personal` does not work there), so the default design runs everything that needs no Editor on a hosted
runner, and runs Editor tests locally or on a machine the user hosts. This document is self-contained.
It does not commit, push, register a runner, or store a secret. **Last verified: October 2026** (Git
2.54, .NET SDK 10.0, Unity CLI 1.0.0-beta.13, Unity 6000.7.0b4 and 6000.6.2f1).

Source (replace `main` with a commit SHA for a repeatable run):
`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/krogh-jacobsen/unity-code-style-guide/main/AuditInstructions/ContinuousIntegration/`

## What each tier does

| Tier | Runs where | Needs a Unity licence | Catches |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A. Project checks** (default) | GitHub-hosted runner | No | Missing/orphan metadata, duplicate GUIDs, static test-isolation candidates, ignored-test notices, Git settings, whitespace and naming violations |
| **B. Local test gate** (default) | The developer's machine | Their own | Failing EditMode and PlayMode tests, through `unity test` and a pull request checklist |
| **C. Self-hosted test runner** (opt-in) | A machine the user owns | Their own, already active | The same tests, run on every pull request |
| **D. Licensed hosted CI** (opt-in) | GitHub-hosted runner | Yes: a serial, floating, or offline licence | Tests and player builds. Use `unity ci init`, not these files |

Tier A never runs the Editor, so **a green run does not mean tests pass**. Say so wherever you report it.

## Operating rules

- Never write a licence, serial, token, or password into a workflow or file. Tier A uses no secrets.
- Do not enable Tier C on a public repository without the user's explicit approval of the risk below.
- Copy the shipped files unchanged except for the documented edit points. Do not commit or push.
- Report observed results separately from checks you could not run (**Not verified**).
- Recommendation IDs retain the meaning of the actual prior proposal. The tier IDs below are
  defaults for a new audit, not replacements for an existing approved change list. On resume,
  recover the exact files/settings/commands before planning execution; missing details remain
  Not verified while unchanged authorization is preserved; continue independent read-only preflight
  while recovering that scope. Do not infer Tier A merely from `R1`.
- Without Unity CLI, continue the saved-file audit. For confirmed execution, run the Python/Git/.NET
  checks directly when those tools exist; mark only unavailable checks Not verified. Authorized
  Editor suites can use the Test Runner window instead of `unity test`. No CLI/bridge installation
  is implied by this workflow.

## Review, recommend, confirm

This document always runs in four stages. Nothing is written to the project until stage 4 ends in an
explicit user confirmation.

1. **Audit.** Read the project and report what already matches this document, what differs, and what
   could not be checked. Read-only.
2. **Recommend.** List every difference as a numbered recommendation: ID, finding, proposed change,
   why it matters, risk (low, medium, high), and a default (do or skip). List items that already
   match as "no change needed". Add recommendations of your own from what you found, including ones
   this document does not mention.
3. **Choose.** The user picks any subset of IDs, "all recommended", or none. Carry over only the
   picked items; unpicked items stay proposals in the report.
4. **Confirm.** Present the exact changes for the picked subset (files, settings, values, commands)
   and obtain explicit user authorization before making them, including saving the report.
   Confirmation need not contain the literal word "yes": after the concrete scope is presented,
   "implement R1 and R3" can both select and confirm those items. Selection alone ("R1 and R3")
   chooses scope without authorizing implementation. Honor existing authorization for unchanged
   scope without asking again; clarify a delayed reply only when its scope is materially ambiguous.
   Resolve IDs against the presented change list rather than guide defaults. If evidence establishes
   that exact scope was previously presented and authorized but its record is now unavailable,
   retrieve that record before execution; recovered unchanged scope needs no repeat confirmation.
   If concrete changes were never presented, an instruction to implement an ID leaves scope
   unconfirmed: first present the exact changes and obtain confirmation before execution.
   Changed scope needs confirmation for the changed items. In a non-interactive session, or when
   authorization is absent, stop after stage 2 and change nothing.

Steps below that apply, install, or build run only after stage 4, and only for confirmed items. A new
finding during those steps becomes a new recommendation and returns to stage 3.

## 1. Preflight

This step is the audit input and changes nothing. Identify one Unity project and its repository. Record:

- The **host**. The workflows are GitHub Actions. For another host, install the scripts only and say the
  workflow is not provided (`unity ci init --provider gitlab` covers GitLab for licensed projects).
- **Project root versus repository root.** Tier A takes the project path from `UNITY_PROJECT_PATH`.
- Existing `.github/workflows/`, `.github/unity-ci/`, and `.github/pull_request_template.md`.
- An **`.editorconfig`** in the project or repository root. The style checks measure against it, so if it
  is missing, install the [EditorConfig starter](../../AgentsInstructions/CodeStyleGuide/EditorConfig/README.md) first or skip the style steps.
- Whether the repository is public or private, and `unity license status` on this machine.
- Whether tests exist (`Assets/**/Tests`, test asmdefs). Follow the [test setup guide](../Testing/TestingInstructions.md)
  when they do not.
- How each existing file compares with its shipped version. Fetch the shipped files into a temporary
  folder outside the project (not a project change) and mark each destination absent, identical, or
  different.

**Done:** host, roots, existing files and their comparison, `.editorconfig`, visibility, and test
presence are known, and the audit was shown to the user.

## 2. Ask and select

Ask in one batch, then show each tier as a numbered recommendation (stage 2) so the user can pick any
subset. The defaults below are recommended defaults: they still need the stage 4 confirmation. Apply
the default when the user says "use defaults".

| ID | Question | Recommended default |
|---|---|---|
| R1 | Tier A (licence-free GitHub checks)? | Do |
| R2 | Tier B (pull request template with a test checklist)? | Do |
| R3 | Tier C (self-hosted test workflow)? | Skip. Needs a runner you register, and the security note in the workflow |
| R4 | Style steps blocking from the first run, or report-only until the baseline is clean? | Report-only when the baseline run in step 4 has findings |

Add your own recommendations from the audit, such as a missing `.editorconfig` or a conflicting workflow.

**Done:** the audit and recommendation list were shown, the user's picks are recorded, and an explicit
user authorization for the exact file list was received before any change.

## 3. Install

Only the items confirmed in stage 4. Stage the files, check them, then copy. Files install to these destinations:

| Source | Destination | Tier |
|---|---|---|
| `Workflows/unity-checks.yml` | `.github/workflows/unity-checks.yml` | A |
| `Scripts/check_unity_project.py` | `.github/unity-ci/check_unity_project.py` | A |
| `Scripts/Lint.csproj` | `.github/unity-ci/Lint.csproj` | A |
| `Workflows/pull_request_template.md` | `.github/pull_request_template.md` | B |
| `Workflows/unity-tests-self-hosted.yml` | `.github/workflows/unity-tests-self-hosted.yml` | C |

1. **Stage** into a temporary folder and reject HTML or error responses.
2. **Destinations.** Absent: install. Identical: leave it. Different content: a conflict. Show both and
   resolve it before copying; never overwrite a project's own workflow or template.
3. **Edit points**, and only these: `UNITY_PROJECT_PATH` in both selected workflow files when the
   project is a repository subfolder (and the matching `Lint.csproj` exclusions if the project has more vendor or
   sample folders); the `branches:` list when the default branch is not `main`.
4. If the style gate is report-only, add `continue-on-error: true` to the two `dotnet format` steps and
   say that is temporary.

**Done:** every confirmed file is installed or identical, and the edit points are the only differences.

## 4. Run the checks locally first

Applies to the installed tiers only. A new gate often fails on the existing code. Learn the baseline before the first push. Run from the repository
root (where `.github/` lives), exporting the absolute Unity project path, including any subfolder:

```bash
export UNITY_PROJECT_PATH="/absolute/repository/path/to/UnityProject"
python3 .github/unity-ci/check_unity_project.py --project "$UNITY_PROJECT_PATH"
unity vcs doctor "$UNITY_PROJECT_PATH"
dotnet restore .github/unity-ci/Lint.csproj
dotnet format whitespace .github/unity-ci/Lint.csproj --no-restore --verify-no-changes
dotnet format style .github/unity-ci/Lint.csproj --no-restore --diagnostics IDE1006 --severity info --verify-no-changes
```

Read each exit code. `unity vcs doctor` exits 4 on a finding. `dotnet format` exits 2 when it would
change something. Report the count per check. Offer to fix formatting with
`dotnet format whitespace <Lint.csproj>`, but only on the user's own code and only with approval: it
rewrites files. Without the .NET SDK or the Unity CLI locally, report those checks as **Not verified**.

**Done:** each check has a baseline result, and the style-gate mode is chosen from it.

## 5. The local test gate (Tier B, only when confirmed)

The pull request template tells reviewers what was run. The commands are in the
[test setup guide](../Testing/TestingInstructions.md):

```bash
unity test /absolute/project --mode EditMode --output /absolute/results/editmode.xml
unity test /absolute/project --mode PlayMode --output /absolute/results/playmode.xml
```

Close the project in the Editor first. Exit code 8 means tests failed; 6 means the run itself failed.
Read the result XML, not just the exit code. Run them now if the user agrees, and report passed,
failed, skipped, and `[Ignore]`d counts from the files.

**Done:** the user has the commands, and the suites were run or the gap is stated.

## 6. The self-hosted workflow (Tier C, only when confirmed)

Registering a runner is the user's action: it needs a token from their repository settings. Give these steps and do
not perform them.

1. Settings > Actions > Runners > New self-hosted runner, on the machine that has the Editor, and add the
   label `unity`.
2. The runner service must run as the user whose Editor licence is active. `unity license status` must show it.
3. Set the workflow's `UNITY_PROJECT_PATH` to the intended project under `${{ github.workspace }}`.
   Its `ProjectVersion.txt` selects the required installed Editor; the project must not be open in it.
   Preflight runs in that directory, and both test commands name it explicitly.
4. **Security.** A self-hosted runner executes the code of whatever it checks out. The workflow is limited
   to branches in the same repository and manual dispatch. Keep the repository private, or understand
   that a contributor with write access can run code on that machine.
5. Run the workflow once with **Run workflow** (`workflow_dispatch`) and read the uploaded results.

**Done:** the steps were given, and the first run is observed by the user or reported as **Not verified**.

## 7. Verify

- The Tier A files match the source, and `.github/unity-ci/` holds both scripts.
- Step 4's commands ran (or are reported **Not verified**).
- The workflow files are valid YAML and contain no secret or licence reference.
- A real GitHub run needs a push, which only the user approves. After one, read the run summary: it
  lists errors and states that Editor tests did not run. Until then report the hosted run as **Not verified**.

**Done:** each installed tier has a verification result or a specific Not verified reason.

## 8. Report

| Item | Status | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| Source URL and revision | | |
| Recommendations picked and confirmed | R-IDs applied | The exact change list the user confirmed |
| Recommendations not picked | Proposal | R-IDs left open, with the default and risk |
| Tier A files | Installed / Identical / Conflict | Paths |
| Tier B template | Installed / Identical / Declined | |
| Tier C workflow | Installed / Declined | Runner registered by the user? |
| Baseline per check | Pass / N findings / Not verified | meta and tests, doctor, whitespace, naming |
| Style gate mode | Blocking / Report-only | |
| Editor tests | Run locally / Not run | Counts from the result files |
| Hosted run | Observed / Not verified | |

Put conflicts, a failing baseline, the unpicked recommendations, and the Tier C security choice in a
"Needs your decision" block at the top. Say plainly that Tier A does not run tests.

**Done:** every selected tier and unpicked recommendation is accounted for, including hosted-run limits.

## For users with a licence

Use `unity ci init` (`--provider github` or `gitlab`, `--shards N` to split tests) instead of these
workflows. It generates a complete pipeline: it installs the Editor, restores caches, activates a
licence, runs tests, and builds. Its licence step takes a serial, a floating server, or an offline
licence file as a secret, and it states that `--personal` activation does not work in CI. Tier A files
still complement it as the fast first job.

# Review and reorganize an existing project's folders (agent instructions)

Compare a project that already has content and its own folder structure against the layout below,
recommend improvements, and, only when the user opts in, move content in small reversible batches.
This document is self-contained. For a brand-new project, use [SetupFolders.md](SetupFolders.md)
instead. **Last verified: October 2026.**

## Operating rules

- Start in **review** mode: read and report only. Move nothing until the user has picked items and
  confirmed the exact batch list (stages 3 and 4 below).
- Move imported assets only through Editor APIs (`AssetDatabase.ValidateMoveAsset`, then
  `AssetDatabase.MoveAsset`) or the Project window. Unity ties references to the GUID in each
  `.meta` file, and moving files outside the Editor risks disconnecting the GUID from the file.
  Treat a non-empty string returned by `MoveAsset` as a failure and stop.
- Checkpoints apply to confirmed move batches, not to read-only audit. Continue independent audit
  with user edits and unsaved scenes preserved. Before a move batch, agree a reversible checkpoint
  and resolve edits that overlap its paths; do not stash, commit, or save unrelated work.
- Leave `Packages/`, `ProjectSettings/`, and vendor content with a required layout where they are.
- Keep a move log (old path, new path, GUID) in the conversation; it is the rollback record.
- On resume, recommendation IDs refer to the actual previously presented batch. Recover its
  old/new paths, owner, checkpoint, and permitted commands before planning moves or commits.
  Missing scope remains Not verified; preserve unchanged authorization and continue independent
  read-only inventory rather than inferring a move batch from `R1` or from this guide's examples.
- Stop at the first error, compile failure, or unexpected change. Report it; never push through.
- Mark checks you cannot run **Not verified**.

## Review, recommend, confirm

This document always runs in four stages. Nothing is written to the project until stage 4 ends in an
explicit user confirmation.

1. **Audit.** Read the project and report what already matches this document, what differs, and what
   could not be checked. Read-only.
2. **Recommend.** List every difference as a numbered recommendation: ID, finding, proposed change,
   why it matters, risk (low, medium, high), and a default (do or skip). List items that already
   match as "no change needed". Add recommendations of your own from what you found, including ones
   this document does not mention.
3. **Choose.** The user picks any subset of IDs, "all recommended", or none. Carry over only the
   picked items; unpicked items stay proposals in the report.
4. **Confirm.** Present the exact changes for the picked subset (files, settings, values, commands)
   and obtain explicit user authorization before making them, including saving the report.
   Confirmation need not contain the literal word "yes": after the concrete scope is presented,
   "implement R1 and R3" can both select and confirm those items. Selection alone ("R1 and R3")
   chooses scope without authorizing implementation. Honor existing authorization for unchanged
   scope without asking again; clarify a delayed reply only when its scope is materially ambiguous.
   Resolve IDs against the presented change list rather than guide defaults. If evidence establishes
   that exact scope was previously presented and authorized but its record is now unavailable,
   retrieve that record before execution; recovered unchanged scope needs no repeat confirmation.
   If concrete changes were never presented, an instruction to implement an ID leaves scope
   unconfirmed: first present the exact changes and obtain confirmation before execution.
   Changed scope needs confirmation for the changed items. In a non-interactive session, or when
   authorization is absent, stop after stage 2 and change nothing.

Steps below that apply, install, or build run only after stage 4, and only for confirmed items. A new
finding during those steps becomes a new recommendation and returns to stage 3.

## 1. Preflight

Read the project's own instructions first; they win over this document. Then record:

- Editor version and whether the Editor is open. Moves need the Editor (or an Editor-driven CLI
  command); a review alone can read the files directly.
- Source-control state, and whether the project compiles cleanly now. Do not start moves on a
  project with compile errors.
- Existing test/compile evidence: record revision, freshness, and known failures. Missing evidence
  is Not verified; new test or compilation runs belong in the confirmed execution plan.
- The `Assets` tree to three levels, with file counts and the longest asset path.
- Template leftovers (`Assets/Settings`, sample scene and assets), vendor folders (Asset Store or
  package-style content with its own layout), and any `Resources`, `StreamingAssets`, `Plugins`,
  `Editor`, or `Gizmos` folders and where they sit.
- Assembly definitions and references, and each script's effective assembly.

**Done:** the inventory and baseline exist, you can state which parts you will treat as vendor, and
nothing has been changed.

## 2. Ask

Ask in one batch. The defaults are recommended answers that still need stages 3 and 4, even when the
user says "use defaults".

| Question | Default |
|---|---|
| Review only, or also reorganize? | Review only |
| Whole project or specific folders or features? | Whole `Assets`, owned content only |
| Adopt the whole layout or only parts? | Parts: keep the project's convention where it is consistent, and fix inconsistencies |
| Move scripts and asmdefs? | No: propose them, move only after separate approval |
| Move path-dependent content (`Resources`, Addressables, `StreamingAssets`)? | No |
| Checkpoint method (commit or stash)? | Commit |

**Done:** the mode and scope are agreed and repeated back in one line each.

## 3. Review against the layout

The target layout, as a menu rather than a mandate:

```text
ArtSource/                # Optional, beside Assets: PSD, Blend, other source files
Packages/                 # Reusable code as embedded packages
Assets/
├── ScriptTemplates/  StreamingAssets/  ThirdPartyAssets/   # direct children when used
├── Settings/Presets/     # Import presets (the starter's convention)
└── {ProjectName}/
    ├── Scenes/  Settings/  Shared/  SceneTemplates/
    └── {Feature}/        # Scenes, Scripts, Editor, Tests, Data, Prefabs, Art, UI
```

Check each area, citing a path as evidence for every finding:

| Area | Look for |
|---|---|
| Organization | Type-first folders (`Scripts`, `Prefabs` at the root) instead of feature-first; duplicate or ambiguous roots (`Scripts` and `Code`); loose assets in the `Assets` root |
| Naming | Spaces, mixed casing, case-only duplicates, dot-prefixed names (Unity skips them on import), accidental `~` suffixes |
| Depth and paths | Nesting beyond about four levels below the content root; very long asset paths |
| Ownership | Content under a feature that other features own, and `Shared` content that depends on feature code or assets; dependency cycles between features |
| Special folders | `StreamingAssets` or `ScriptTemplates` not direct children of `Assets`; `Resources` used for convenience instead of a loading need; `Plugins`, `Editor`, or `Gizmos` placed where they change compilation or behavior |
| Assemblies | Scripts outside any intended asmdef; `Editor` folders inside runtime asmdefs without Editor-only assemblies; test asmdefs that cannot reference production assemblies |
| Vendor content | Vendor files mixed with owned content; vendor files modified in place |
| Source art | PSD, Blend, or other source files inside `Assets` |
| Template leftovers | Unused sample scenes and assets |

Rate each finding **Risk** (likely to cause bugs or build failures), **Improve** (clear benefit), or
**Optional** (taste), and give its **move risk** from the next table.

### Move risk

Moves are safe when only GUIDs refer to the asset, and dangerous where a path, folder name, or
folder position carries meaning.

| Move risk | Content | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Low | Prefabs, materials, textures, models, audio, ScriptableObject assets, UI files, and scenes, moved between ordinary folders | Unity references them by GUID, and the Editor moves the `.meta` file with the asset |
| Medium | Scripts, asmdefs, asmrefs, and anything moved into or out of an `Editor`, `Plugins`, or `Standard Assets` folder | Folder position selects the compile phase and assembly, and an asmdef covers the whole folder tree beneath it, so a move can change which assembly a script belongs to |
| High | `Resources` contents, Addressables, `StreamingAssets` contents, hard-coded `"Assets/..."` strings, import presets and postprocessors scoped by path, CI and `.gitignore` or LFS patterns | Their meaning depends on the path text. Unity's Addressables default address is the asset path, so a moved asset's address can change |
| Leave | `Packages/`, `ProjectSettings/`, vendor content with a required layout, template-created `Assets/Settings`, `Editor Default Resources`, and the special folders themselves | Unity or the vendor expects them where they are |

Before rating anything Medium or High, search the project for `Resources.Load`, hard-coded `Assets/`
paths, Addressables addresses, and path-scoped presets, and record what you find.

**Done:** every finding has evidence, a severity, and a move risk, and every High item has the
code or configuration that depends on it listed. The findings are the audit stage's output.

## 4. Recommend and plan

Present the review: a short summary, the findings table, and what to leave alone, with each finding
as a numbered recommendation (ID, evidence, proposed change, risk, default). Then offer a plan
only if the user asked to reorganize, as ordered batches:

1. Create missing target folders (follow the naming rules: PascalCase, no spaces, no leading dot).
2. Rename and case fixes. On a case-insensitive file system, move a case-only rename through a
   temporary name, and check the result in the Editor.
3. Low-risk content, one feature at a time.
4. Scripts and asmdefs, one assembly at a time (only if approved).
5. High-risk items, only on explicit request and with a stated verification for each.

Each batch lists its moves (old path → new path), the expected effect, the risk, the checks that
prove it, and how to undo it. Keep batches small enough to review: one feature or one assembly.

**Done:** the user has picked specific recommendations and confirmed the exact batches in stage 4,
or chosen review only. The per-batch checkpoints in step 5 stay as extra safety on top of that gate.

## 5. Apply one batch at a time

Only the items confirmed in stage 4 are moved. For each confirmed batch:

1. Checkpoint, then run `ValidateMoveAsset` for every move; resolve any non-empty result first.
2. Move through `MoveAsset`, requiring an empty return each time. Run `AssetDatabase.SaveAssets` and
   `Refresh`, and wait for compilation to finish.
3. Verify (step 6). On success, commit the batch with the move log in the message.
4. On any failure, undo the batch by moving the assets back through `MoveAsset` using the move log.
   If the Editor state is unreliable, close it and restore the checkpoint with source control.

**Done:** the audit and recommendation list were shown and confirmed before batch 1, and the batch is
committed with verification passed, or fully undone with the cause reported.

## 6. Verify each batch

- Every moved asset keeps its GUID (`AssetDatabase.AssetPathToGUID` before and after).
- The project compiles with no new errors, and each moved script's effective assembly is unchanged
  (compare before and after, for example with `CompilationPipeline.GetAssemblyNameFromScriptPath`).
- Open the scenes and prefabs of the affected features: no missing references or scripts.
- The build scene list still points at existing scenes. Check it; do not assume it updated.
- The project's tests pass, matching the baseline, and Play Mode starts the affected scenes.
- Path-dependent items found in step 3 still resolve: `Resources.Load` names, string paths,
  Addressables addresses, preset and postprocessor filters, CI and ignore patterns.
- After script or assembly batches, a build for a representative player target compiles.

**Done:** each check is Passed, Failed, or Not verified, and any failure has been undone or fixed.

## 7. Report

| Item | Status | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| Each finding | Risk / Improve / Optional | Path, evidence, recommendation, move risk |
| Unpicked recommendations | Proposal | ID and reason left open |
| Each batch | Applied / Undone / Not started | Moves, commit, checks |
| Each check | Passed / Failed / Not verified | Evidence |
| Left alone | Vendor / Leave | Path and reason |

Put open questions, unpicked recommendations that need a ruling, and failed checks in a
"Needs your decision" block at the top.

  is selected. These lenses win over any older copies in the project; a project's own audit guide
  runs alongside them only when the user names it. Cross-links between lenses name the owner of a
  check: follow one only when the finding needs it.

This document always runs in four stages. Nothing is written to the project until stage 4 ends in an
explicit user confirmation.

1. **Audit.** Read the project and report what already matches this document, what differs, and what
   could not be checked. Read-only.
2. **Recommend.** List every difference as a numbered recommendation: ID, finding, proposed change,

   picked items; unpicked items stay proposals in the report.
4. **Confirm.** Present the exact changes for the picked subset (files, settings, values, commands)
   and obtain explicit user authorization before making them, including saving the report.
   Confirmation need not contain the literal word "yes": after the concrete scope is presented,
   "implement R1 and R3" can both select and confirm those items. Selection alone ("R1 and R3")
   chooses scope without authorizing implementation. Honor existing authorization for unchanged
   scope without asking again; clarify a delayed reply only when its scope is materially ambiguous.
   Resolve IDs against the presented change list rather than guide defaults. If evidence establishes
   that exact scope was previously presented and authorized but its record is now unavailable,
   retrieve that record before execution; recovered unchanged scope needs no repeat confirmation.
   If concrete changes were never presented, an instruction to implement an ID leaves scope
   unconfirmed: first present the exact changes and obtain confirmation before execution.
   Changed scope needs confirmation for the changed items. In a non-interactive session, or when
   authorization is absent, stop after stage 2 and change nothing.

Steps below that apply, install, or build run only after stage 4, and only for confirmed items. A new
finding during those steps becomes a new recommendation and returns to stage 3.

How the stages map onto the steps below, and the two different picks:
- Steps 1, 3, and 4 are stage 1 (audit).
- Step 2 is a pick of **which reviews to run**: a read-only scope choice, not stage 3.
- Step 5 holds stages 2, 3, and 4: recommend, pick **which fixes to carry over**, and confirm.
- Step 6 applies, and runs only after stage 4.

## 1. Preflight: sources, scope, and what the project contains

Locate the project's `AGENTS.md`, style guide, `.editorconfig`, and setup or audit guides; the
[style guide](../../AgentsInstructions/CodeStyleGuide/UnityStyleGuide.md) in this starter is the default for naming and
organization, and the [setup index](../SetupInstructions/README.md) is the default only for the
structure-and-settings base check. Missing sources leave the affected conformance checks Not
verified; continue independent review rather than substituting remembered rules.

Record the scope (the user's folder, change, or whole project; if unspecified, state the first-party
scope and the exclusions), the base revision for a change review, starting branch/commit, and an
inventory of staged, unstaged, and untracked files (or the available non-Git source identity). Record
engine and package versions, platform, and selected stack. First-party means everything under `Assets` except
vendor, sample, and generated folders (include project folders such as `Assets/Settings` and
`Editor`), plus embedded packages the team owns; read the folder names and `AGENTS.md` to decide, and
state the result. Check whether an Editor has the project open (`Temp/UnityLockfile`) and say so,
because unsaved scenes must be preserved. Ask only when an unresolved choice materially changes the
review.

Then detect what the project contains, using the signals in the [lens table](#2-choose-the-reviews).
Apply the scope's exclusions to detection as well: count first-party content only (vendor packages,
samples, and generated folders excluded), and state the raw and first-party counts when they differ.
Search by file listing, manifest, and text search first, quoting paths (project folders contain
spaces; use `find -print0` or `grep -r`). If `unity-cli` is unavailable or the user forbids it,
inventory components from saved scenes and prefabs by YAML class ID (enough for detection; use script
GUIDs only to identify a specific component type) instead, and record the live checks Not verified. Record for each lens the evidence you found, or "nothing
detected".

**Done:** scope, versions, and the source documents are recorded, and every lens has detection
evidence or "nothing detected", and detected systems without a matching lens are listed Outside coverage.

## 2. Choose the reviews

Show the user one menu, headed by the scope, exclusions, engine and package versions, and the binding
project choices from `AGENTS.md` that bear on the lenses, one line each. Label every lens:
- **Recommended**: a strong signal, meaning a component, asset, or API used in first-party runtime
  content or code.
- **Optional**: a weak or partial signal (found only in tools, tests, or imported model prefabs, or one
  lone asset), or a strong signal where a documented project policy limits the lens.
- **Not detected**: no signal. Record it as Not applicable in the report.

List the base checks and the integrity pass as included, each lens with its evidence. The integrity pass is Part A of the Editor tooling file and
Part B is a separate lens. Offer these shortcuts and accept any custom subset:

| Shortcut | Runs |
|---|---|
| Quick health check | Integrity pass, base checks, Performance, Scenes and lifecycle, Assets and memory |
| Full review | Integrity pass, base checks, and every lens marked Recommended |
| Custom | Exactly the lenses the user names, including a Not detected one when they insist |

A narrow request (a button edit, a single subsystem) selects only the behavior it touches and its
dependencies, so do not load the whole folder. If the user already named the lenses, confirm the list
and go on. If no one can answer the menu (a non-interactive session), run the Quick health check,
which is read-only, and stop after stage 2.

### Detected systems outside lens coverage

During detection, also inventory the following signals within the same first-party scope. Record
**Outside coverage** with evidence and consequence, rather than treating an uncovered system as
Not applicable or reviewed by a neighboring lens. Package presence alone is a weak signal: separate
installed capability from first-party usage. This inventory does not add or load a new lens.

| System | Detection evidence | Review limit |
|---|---|---|
| DOTS Physics | Unity Physics/Havok packages plus owned physics-world, collision-event or solver code | Entities covers generic ECS ordering/ECB safety; no DOTS contact/solver lens |

| Specialist services/content | Backend/economy/IAP, XR, custom AI, procedural generators or third-party systems beyond stated rows | Name the actual system and specialist security, platform or authoring checks not performed |
| Other first-party systems | Content/code with no matching lens, found while inventorying the project | Name the system and the absent review; do not infer exhaustive coverage from the menu |

For each detected uncovered system, list the owning files/assets, applicable generic checks, and the
specific specialist work not performed. Offer a separate scoped review against installed official
docs when the user wants it. **Full review** means all selected applicable lenses, not all possible
subsystem risks. Include this coverage boundary in the menu and final report.

Physics2D uses its dedicated lens; DOTS Physics remains outside both classic physics lenses. Use
matching installed documentation for specialist checks. [Debugging](UnityDebuggingInstructions.md) is not an audit lens. It is the
[diagnose mode](#diagnose-a-reported-defect) for a user-reported symptom.

**Done:** the user has picked, or confirmed a shortcut for, the reviews to run, and the list is
recorded with a reason for every lens left out.

## 3. Run the selected reviews

Run the integrity pass first, because asset identity comes before conventions. Inspect vendor metadata
only for database-wide integrity, and exclude vendor and generated source from style review unless
the user scoped it in.

These base checks have no lens of their own; run them in a whole-project review and in the Quick
health check:

| Check family | Source of truth | Evidence to inspect |
|---|---|---|
| Naming and formatting | [Style guide](../../AgentsInstructions/CodeStyleGuide/UnityStyleGuide.md) and project `.editorconfig` | Prefix and casing exceptions, modifiers, fields and properties, braces, actual code |
| Class organization | Project and style guide | Member order, MonoBehaviour and file identity, approved region usage |
| API and stack compatibility | Project tech stack and installed source or official docs | Actual versions, obsolete API availability, selected input, UI, and pipeline |
| Structure and settings | Project rules, [folder review](../FolderStructure/ReviewFolders.md), [project settings](../ProjectSettings/ProjectSettings.md) | Intended folder and settings policy versus actual state |

⚠️ Every search pattern is a candidate. Read the enclosing code and the callers, and honor documented
project choices. Do not report every lambda, every static, a missing asmdef, any `Resources` folder,
or a version-independent API ban list as a finding. Confirm the actual failure or the binding rule.

Then load each selected lens, one at a time, and record **Checked**, **Finding**, **Not applicable**,
or **Not verified** for each of its rows. State the sample for every lens, and how many files you read
out of how many exist. Cover every file when the check is a search or a count. For rows that need
reading, start with the largest, most recently changed (`git log --since` churn), and highest-risk
owned files.

**Done:** every selected lens and base check has an outcome for each row, with the inspected scope or
sample stated.

## 4. Fill live and test evidence gaps

Use `unity-cli` for Editor inspection and the project's runner for authorized tests; follow any
required test-runner delegation. Read-only queries of the current state do not need repeated
permission when already authorized. Preserve dirty scenes; use saved-asset inspection or isolated
scenes for checks that need different content. Obtain new authorization before any additional
disruptive live action.

If the Editor, runner, device, or build is unavailable, record the specific checks **Not verified**
and continue static work. In a static-only run, state each lens's live-only rows once as **Not
verified (live)** with the checks to run later, instead of repeating it row by row. Parse fresh test
results and logs, and distinguish failures, exclusions, and not-run tests.

For each runtime evidence collection, record scene/content identity, Play state, compilation/reload
state, activity (gameplay, script recompilation, preview, or test fixture), log cursor or timestamp
range, and source revision plus relevant dirty-file state. Record shared context once and differences
per finding. Retain supplied or measured context as known; mark only unavailable fields Not verified.
An exception establishes what occurred in that
context; check whether it was expected by a test or preview before calling it a product defect.
Its cause remains a hypothesis until supporting evidence distinguishes alternatives.

- ❌ Do not call an unopened prefab correct from source alone.
- ❌ Do not claim a live repair is saved.

**Done:** each live or test check has fresh evidence and its collection context, or is listed Not
verified with its reason and any unavailable context.

## 5. Report and recommend

Separate confirmed defects, measured costs, convention drift, and design proposals. Each finding
meets the [evidence standard](#evidence-standard). Group one repeated cause with counts and
representative locations, and list every affected duplicate-GUID pair. Record conflicts and limits,
including inspected samples, systems Outside coverage, and whether the live, test, and build checks ran.

Put material observations encountered outside selected lenses in **Incidental observations**, with
location, evidence, consequence, and the narrow inspection performed. Inspect only enough to explain
the observation; offer further investigation as a separate scope choice. An incidental observation
does not mark that lens reviewed or authorize a fix.

Then turn the findings into the numbered recommendations of stage 2: for each, the smallest useful
fix, intended outcome, checkable acceptance condition, validation method and known constraints, why
it matters, its risk, and a default of do or skip. Let the user pick any subset (stage 3), then apply
the shared confirmation rules to its exact changes (stage 4). Ask whether
to save the report as a file and where; saving is itself a change and waits for stage 4.

**Done:** the report distinguishes selected-lens findings from incidental observations, every
recommendation has an acceptance condition and validation method, and the user's selection and
confirmation status are explicit; nothing was written before authorization.

## 6. Apply confirmed fixes

Apply only the items confirmed in stage 4. Before editing each item's target files, re-read them and
check that its supporting evidence and approved scope still apply. Recheck affected source before
validation and record the state actually validated. A branch/commit change or relevant dirty edit
requires reassessment of affected findings; unrelated edits do not restart the audit. Mark explicitly
assigned work in another chat **Externally owned** and exclude it from edits unless handed over;
a dirty file alone does not establish ownership. Preserve concurrent changes and re-confirm changed
scope under the shared contract.

Selected fixes preserve serialized identity and follow the matching implementation skill or project
workflow. Report each selected item with separate implementation and acceptance results:

| Item | Implemented change | Acceptance result | Remaining validation |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | Missing-session guard added | Not verified | Recompile during Play and exercise callbacks |

Run relevant validation against the agreed acceptance condition. Compilation establishes compatibility,
not gameplay recovery. An item can be implemented while its behavior remains Not verified; close it
as resolved only when its acceptance conditions pass. Name missing checks and their tooling,
authorization, or environment constraints. Attribute results to the actual source state; mixed-revision
validation cannot establish that a single commit passed.

**Done:** every selected item records its implementation state, acceptance evidence or Not verified
with the missing check and constraint, and validated source state where applicable; externally owned
items are identified, and every unpicked recommendation remains a proposal. Unverified acceptance
keeps the item open even when the implementation work is done.

## Diagnose a reported defect

When the user hands over a symptom (a bug, a build-only failure, a repeated-Play problem) instead of a
review scope, use [the diagnosis guide](UnityDebuggingInstructions.md): capture the failing context,
route the symptom to the owning lens above, and follow its reproduce, hypothesize, probe, fix, and
regression-test loop. The same read-only and confirm-before-change rules apply.

## Evidence standard

A search hit is a candidate. Read the enclosing code, callers, ownership, and applicable settings
before reporting it. A checklist row names a risk to investigate, not an automatic defect: multiple
writers, polling, an ignored return value, a shared asset, or an optional optimization can be valid.
Establish a broken behavior/resource contract, measured budget failure, or binding project-rule
violation; otherwise label a justified improvement as a proposal with its tradeoff. Official API
semantics support technical claims; architecture preferences and starting budgets remain project
choices. Record source/version and the limits of the evidence rather than treating an official
recommendation as universally optimal. Follow per-frame helper calls; inspect release, cancellation, and failure paths.
Exclude generated and vendor code from style review unless scoped in. Vendor metadata may still
matter to a project-wide GUID integrity check.

For each selected check family or lens, record **Checked**, **Finding**, **Not applicable**, or
**Not verified**. State the inspected scope or sample and any missing evidence.

⚠️ Static inspection does not establish runtime behavior, target-device performance, or correct
saved scene and prefab wiring.

A finding needs:
- **Location** and **trigger**
- **Observed evidence** and **consequence**; runtime observations carry the collection context from step 4
- **Cause assessment**, for diagnostic findings: established, suspected, or unknown, with supporting evidence
- **Governing source**: a project rule or a technical source
- **Smallest useful fix**, **intended outcome**, and **checkable acceptance condition**
- **Validation method** and **known constraints**

A reproduced runtime failure is not required for an inspected static defect, convention drift, or
design proposal; label the finding's evidence and category accurately. For diagnostic fixes,
distinguish containment from recovery: suppressing an invalid callback and restoring a running game
after recompilation have different acceptance conditions. A symptom disappearing alone does not
establish the proposed cause.

Rank confirmed corruption, data loss, bugs, and leaks ahead of measured performance problems; label
convention drift and design proposals separately. Combine repeated instances of one cause while
preserving affected locations.

The review is complete when every selected check family and lens has an outcome, each finding has
inspected evidence, and unverified work is explicit. A clean static review means no confirmed findings
in that scope; it does not imply unperformed runtime checks passed.

## Maintenance

- ✅ Keep one owner per check: general frame cost in Performance, rendering correctness in Rendering, resource residency in Assets, async
  lifetime and destroyed-object checks in Scenes, command ownership in Design, persisted state in
  Persistence, UI and world input arbitration in Input, test inclusion in Assemblies. Other lenses
  link there and add only subsystem-specific failure cases.
- ✅ Keep each lens focused on one recurring risk. Add a lens only for a distinct recurring risk with a
  detection signal and a clear loading condition; update the table above, the readme, and `AGENTS.md`
  together.
- ✅ Keep existing lens filenames stable for consumers.
- ✅ Verify version-sensitive claims against engine or package source or official Unity docs, link
  official docs by unversioned URL, and keep each lens's `Last verified` line current.
- ❌ Keep tutorial examples, historical project class names, and review logs outside this folder.

> How it works: give this URL to your agent, for example "Install the starter script templates in my
> Unity project from this document". The agent audits your project first and recommends
> templates, lets you pick which to carry over, and changes nothing before you confirm the exact
> list. It then copies the templates you picked into `Assets/ScriptTemplates/`, confirms Unity picked
> them up, and reports what it verified. Human overview: [readme](README.md).

# Set up script templates (agent instructions)

Install selected script templates (`.cs.txt` files that Unity offers in the Create menu) into an
existing Unity project. This document is self-contained and installs template text only: no
generated gameplay scripts, packages, asmdefs, or project settings. **Last verified: October 2026**
(Unity 6000.7.0b4; the Static Event template also on 6000.6.2f1).

Source (replace `main` with a commit SHA for a repeatable run):
`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/krogh-jacobsen/unity-code-style-guide/main/AuditInstructions/ScriptTemplates/`
Each template is two files, `<name>.cs.txt` and `<name>.cs.txt.meta`. Filenames contain spaces, so
URL-encode them. The license is
`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/krogh-jacobsen/unity-code-style-guide/main/LICENSE`.

## Operating rules

- Copy shipped bytes and metadata unchanged. Never author or edit a template or its `.meta`, invent
  GUIDs, rename the files, or delete metadata. The filename sets the menu entry, so a rename moves it.
- Install into the project's `Assets/ScriptTemplates/`, never into the Editor installation: Unity
  overwrites that folder on upgrade.
- Keep a target's different UI, async, or assembly choices; install only templates whose
  prerequisites the project meets, and defer the rest instead of installing packages.
- Report observed results separately from checks you could not run (**Not verified**). A template is a
  text asset: a successful import does not prove the C# it generates compiles.
- Missing recommendation details do not block independent read-only preflight. Inspect the Editor,
  packages, namespace, and existing templates while recovering the prior change list or gathering
  the evidence needed to present concrete changes; keep execution pending until scope is known.

## Review, recommend, confirm

This document always runs in four stages. Nothing is written to the project until stage 4 ends in an
explicit user confirmation.

1. **Audit.** Read the project and report what already matches this document, what differs, and what
   could not be checked. Read-only.
2. **Recommend.** List every difference as a numbered recommendation: ID, finding, proposed change,
   why it matters, risk (low, medium, high), and a default (do or skip). List items that already
   match as "no change needed". Add recommendations of your own from what you found, including ones
   this document does not mention.
3. **Choose.** The user picks any subset of IDs, "all recommended", or none. Carry over only the
   picked items; unpicked items stay proposals in the report.
4. **Confirm.** Present the exact changes for the picked subset (files, settings, values, commands)
   and obtain explicit user authorization before making them, including saving the report.
   Confirmation need not contain the literal word "yes": after the concrete scope is presented,
   "implement R1 and R3" can both select and confirm those items. Selection alone ("R1 and R3")
   chooses scope without authorizing implementation. Honor existing authorization for unchanged
   scope without asking again; clarify a delayed reply only when its scope is materially ambiguous.
   Resolve IDs against the presented change list rather than guide defaults. If evidence establishes
   that exact scope was previously presented and authorized but its record is now unavailable,
   retrieve that record before execution; recovered unchanged scope needs no repeat confirmation.
   If concrete changes were never presented, an instruction to implement an ID leaves scope
   unconfirmed: first present the exact changes and obtain confirmation before execution.
   Changed scope needs confirmation for the changed items. In a non-interactive session, or when
   authorization is absent, stop after stage 2 and change nothing.

Steps below that apply, install, or build run only after stage 4, and only for confirmed items. A new
finding during those steps becomes a new recommendation and returns to stage 3.

Here, steps 1 and 2 are the audit and the recommendations; steps 3 to 5 run only for confirmed items.

## 1. Preflight

Read the target's instructions. Identify one Unity project (the user's destination or the current
workspace, containing `Assets` and `ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt`). Record:

- Editor version, and whether that Editor is open. Unity 6.5 or later is needed for the Static Event
  template as shipped (the attribute is documented from 6.5; tested on 6000.6 and 6000.7; see its row below).
- The Root Namespace (Project Settings > Editor), packages already installed (Test Framework,
  Netcode for GameObjects), and any assembly definitions.
- The contents of `Assets/ScriptTemplates/`, including customized templates.
- The source revision you will use; resolve `main` to a commit when you can.

**Done:** the target, Editor version, namespace, packages, and existing templates are known, and the
audit (stage 1) was reported without writing anything.

Notes on choosing:

- Awaitable Operation is the async pattern: one cancellable operation owned by the component, cancelled on disable, destroy, or restart, with every outcome observed.
- The five defaults need no package and no project-specific base class. Everything else is opt-in.
- Choose one Inspector approach per target: IMGUI (6 to 8) or UI Toolkit (15 to 17). Unity recommends
  UI Toolkit for new Editor UI; IMGUI still works. Drawer and Editor templates are deliberately
  unregistered placeholders: the user adds `[CustomEditor]` or `[CustomPropertyDrawer]` with a real target.
- Test templates are `[Ignore]`d placeholders until real assertions replace them; report them as
  unfinished.
- A retired priority-13 state sketch exists in `ReferenceOnly/`. Do not install it.
- **Static Event compatibility:** the attribute is documented from Unity 6.5; the shipped template
  was compiled on 6000.6.2f1 and 6000.7.0b4. Confirm API/code-generator availability on other patches.
  On an Editor before 6.5, defer this shipped template. If the user separately selects an adapted
  custom template, preserve the shipped pair and create the adaptation through the target
  project's Editor workflow with its own identity. Remove the unavailable lifecycle namespace and
  attribute from that adaptation, and reset its event with:

  ```csharp
  [RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod(RuntimeInitializeLoadType.SubsystemRegistration)]
  private static void ResetStatics()
  {
      EventRaised = null;
  }
  ```

Turn the answers into numbered recommendations (stage 2): one per template worth installing (the five
defaults first, then optional ones whose prerequisites the project meets), one for deferring each
template whose prerequisite is missing, and one for the generation checks. Give each its finding from
the audit, why it matters, risk, and a default. The user may pick any subset (stage 3), then confirms
the exact list (stage 4).

**Done:** the recommendations were shown, the user picked from them, and the selected templates,
deferred prerequisites, and Editor-version decisions were confirmed before any file was written.

## 3. Install

Only the templates confirmed in stage 4. Stage first, then check, then copy.

1. **Stage.** Download each selected `.cs.txt` and `.cs.txt.meta` into a temporary folder outside
   the target's `Assets`, plus the license. Reject HTML or error responses and any half pair.
2. **Verify.** Each `.meta` must contain the `guid:` from the table above. Stop on a mismatch.
3. **Preflight destinations.** Each file installs to `Assets/ScriptTemplates/<filename>` with its
   `.meta` beside it. Reject path traversal, symlinks, and case-only collisions, and check each GUID
   against existing project assets.

   | Destination state | Action |
   |---|---|
   | Absent and the GUID unused | New: install |
   | Same bytes and GUID at the path | Already installed: leave it |
   | Different content or GUID, a half pair, or the GUID elsewhere | Conflict: report both and resolve before copying. A customized template is never overwritten |

4. **Copy.** With the target's Editor closed, create only the missing `Assets/ScriptTemplates/`
   directory and copy the staged pairs intact; Unity generates metadata for the new folder. With the
   Editor open, use an approved route that keeps the pairs together, or ask the user to close it.
5. **License.** Place the MIT license in the project's existing third-party notices location outside
   `Assets`, or at `ThirdPartyNotices/UnityCodeStyleGuide-LICENSE.txt`. Reuse an identical notice.
6. **Read back.** Confirm each installed file's bytes and GUID, and check the import log for fresh
   errors. A repeat run must plan no copies.

**Done:** every selected pair is installed or already present, the license is placed, and a repeat run
does nothing.

## 4. Confirm the Create menu

Unity reads templates when the Editor starts. Restart the target Editor (preserving unsaved work), or
ask the user to, then check that each selected entry appears under Assets > Create > Scripting. File
presence alone does not prove readiness. If a restart or inspection is not possible, report menu
readiness as **Not verified** with the next action.

**Done:** each selected menu entry is observed, or readiness is explicitly pending.

## 5. Generation checks (only when selected and confirmed)

Run in a disposable project or an agreed temporary fixture, and remove it through Editor APIs
afterward. For each selected template:

1. Expand it twice, once with an empty Root Namespace and once with a populated one, using Unity's own
   expansion. Unity's non-public `ProjectWindowUtil.CreateScriptAssetFromTemplate(path, templateFile)`
   works through reflection (verified on 6000.7.0b4); the public `CreateScriptAssetFromTemplateFile`
   is interactive.
2. Place Editor templates in an `Editor` folder or Editor-only assembly, and tests in isolated test
   assemblies.
3. Import, then read the compiler output. Expect zero errors **and zero warnings**: with Enter Play
   Mode set to skip domain reload, the `UAL` analyzer warns about any unprotected static state.
4. Exercise the selected runtime dependencies (a UIDocument with PanelSettings, a pool with an
   inactive prefab, Netcode set up) before claiming the behavior works.

**Done:** each template compiles cleanly under both namespace settings, or the unperformed check is
stated.

## 6. Report

| Item | Status | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| Source URL and revision | | |
| Each selected template | Installed / Already installed / Conflict / Deferred | Path and GUID |
| License | Placed / Already present | Location |
| Repeat run | Nothing to do / Work found | |
| Unity import | Verified / Not verified | |
| Create menu | Observed / Not verified | Next action |
| Generation and compile | Passed / Not selected / Not verified | Editor version, diagnostics |
| Unpicked recommendations | Proposal | IDs, with the reason each was skipped |

Put conflicts, version gates, unanswered choices, and unpicked recommendations in a "Needs your
decision" block at the top.

## Adapting a template

Templates are plain text with Unity substitutions. Keep these when editing a copy in the project:

- `#SCRIPTNAME#` becomes the class name; `#ROOTNAMESPACEBEGIN#` and `#ROOTNAMESPACEEND#` wrap the
  body in the project's Root Namespace, and an empty namespace generates valid code. The whitespace
  before `#ROOTNAMESPACEBEGIN#` sets the indent inside a populated namespace (verified: four spaces
  indent the body one level).
- The filename is `<priority>-<menu path with __ between levels>-<default filename>.cs.txt`.
  Changing it moves or replaces the menu entry.
- Customize in the project, not the Editor installation.
